nodes.label: A fixed verifier goes stale as the agent improves; the disciplined fix is epochs - a fixed within-epoch criterion, utility updated only at epoch boundaries, so guarantees hold per epoch
nodes.description: The Red Queen Godel Machine - Co-Evolving Agents and Their Evaluators (RQGM, arXiv:2606.26294, VERIFIED via arXiv abstract read run 207; June 2026). Self-improving agents' search methods generally assume a STATIONARY evaluation criterion - a fixed verifier, benchmark, or labeled dataset that stays valid as the agent improves. This ignores a central feature of evolution: species adapt as their environments change with them. RQGM makes evaluation part of the improvement loop and opens search to evolving evaluators, adversarial objectives, and dynamic utilities. The mechanism that keeps it sound: CONTROLLED UTILITY EVOLUTION - search is organised into epochs with a FIXED within-epoch evaluation criterion, while the utility can be updated only at epoch boundaries, so self-improvement guarantees hold PER EPOCH as the objective evolves across them. Results: on verifiable coding tasks, adding a complementary agent-as-a-judge code-review signal improves test pass rate over prior SOTA at 1.35x-1.72x fewer tokens; on scientific paper writing/reviewing and Olympiad proof writing/grading, co-evolved writers reach 1.78x-1.86x higher acceptance under a diverse agent-as-a-judge panel and co-evolved graders reach 9% higher ground-truth accuracy; the strongest baseline reviewer over-accepts AI-generated papers at up to 1.91x the human rate, and RQGM corrects this by an adversarial objective that discovers reviewers equally stringent on AI and human work. Bearing on the project: this is the discipline for revising holdout_tasks.py. The current 17-task frozen set is epoch N; a deliberate human edit (with a note) opens epoch N+1; held-out regression claims are only comparable WITHIN an epoch, and sweep docs should record which epoch a run's baseline belongs to. RQGM's anchored co-evolved grader (+9% ground truth) is the constructive complement to Who Grades the Grader's always-pass collapse. Recency/currency: June 2026, RL / Godel-machine framing (the project is emergence-first / no weight training) - the epoch discipline transfers; the RL search does not.

nodes.label: Self-evolving skill libraries silently drift - unbounded accumulation without outcome-driven retirement degrades retrieval; the fix is outcome-driven retirement + a bounded active-cap + a meta-skill authoring prior
nodes.description: Library Drift: Diagnosing and Fixing a Silent Failure Mode in Self-Evolving LLM Skill Libraries (arXiv:2605.19576, VERIFIED via arXiv abstract read run 208; May 2026). LIBRARY DRIFT: unbounded skill accumulation without outcome-driven lifecycle management causes retrieval degradation, false-positive injections, and performance stagnation. The symptom is confirmed - LLM-authored skills deliver +0.0pp gain while human-curated ones deliver +16.2pp (SkillsBench) - but the mechanism had not been isolated. Contributions: (1) a reproducible trigger - ablations that isolate drift: disabling skill injection gives a flat floor (+0.002), imposing premature retirement is actively harmful (-0.019); (2) trace-level diagnostics - an APPEND-ONLY EVIDENCE LOG with per-skill contribution scores, attribution verdicts, and router-engagement metrics that make the failure visible BEFORE it reaches end-task scores; (3) a verified fix - a minimal governance recipe (outcome-driven retirement + bounded active-cap + meta-skill authoring prior) lifting held-out pass@1 from a 0.258 baseline to a late-window mean of 0.584 (rolling gain +0.328) on MBPP+ hard-100 over 100 rounds. Eight ablations decompose which governance mechanisms are load-bearing and which are subsumed. Bearing on the project: this is the published justification for the experience_bank retention API (run 175: utility_score, prune with a grace window, record_use(helped)) and skill_induction.retire() (run 173) - and it adds two things the project does not yet have: a BOUNDED ACTIVE-CAP (not just utility-ranked pruning) and a META-SKILL AUTHORING PRIOR, plus the warning that PREMATURE retirement is worse than none (-0.019), which argues the run-175 grace window should be generous. The append-only per-skill contribution log is a Phase 0 trace-substrate application. Recency: May 2026, MBPP+ / code-agent regime; the drift mechanism is model-agnostic, the pass@1 numbers are task-specific.

nodes.label: Across 930k agent-authored PRs, ~half of integration-friction variation is repository-level and survives full controls; agent contributions concentrate it 2x more than human (ICC 0.30 vs 0.16) - govern the ecosystem, not the agent
nodes.description: Govern the Repository, Not the Agent: Measuring Ecosystem-Level Risk in AI-Native Software (arXiv:2606.28235, VERIFIED via arXiv abstract read run 209; June 2026). Autonomous coding agents open and merge PRs in shared repositories at scale, but the field evaluates them one agent at a time on isolated benchmark tasks - and agents that each pass their own tests still leave repositories that accumulate problems no single contribution accounts for. The study measures INTEGRATION FRICTION (the cost of integrating a contribution into a codebase other contributors are concurrently changing) across MORE THAN 930,000 agent-authored pull requests. About HALF the variation in friction stays with the repository after the contribution, its author, its size, and its agent are all accounted for, and it survives full controls. Agent-authored contributions concentrate this repository-level friction roughly TWICE as much as human ones (intraclass correlation 0.30 vs 0.16), a gap that holds after controlling for codebase size, age, task shape, process maturity, and merge path. Conclusion: the risk is a property of the ECOSYSTEM, not the agent; AI-native software is better measured and governed at the ecosystem level than one agent at a time. This is the project's emergence-first thesis and its governance-grade-measurement niche, stated as a large-N empirical result in the coding-agent domain: single-agent benchmarks miss the accumulating interaction cost; concept_irreversibility_budget's 'fleet-level budget, not a per-act check' is the same claim. Recency: June 2026, current coding-agent generation.

nodes.label: AI-native software ecosystems are complex adaptive systems - architectural entropy, cascade failures, comprehension debt emerge from agent interactions, not components; ecosystem-level monitoring as primary governance
nodes.description: More Is Different: Toward a Theory of Emergence in AI-Native Software Ecosystems (arXiv:2604.19827, VERIFIED via arXiv abstract read run 209; April 2026). Argues AI-native software ecosystems must be studied as COMPLEX ADAPTIVE SYSTEMS (CAS): individual agents perform correctly, but their interactions degrade entire ecosystems, and emergent properties - architectural entropy, cascade failures, comprehension debt - arise from interactions, not components. Maps Holland's six CAS properties onto observable ecosystem dynamics; distinguishes these systems from microservices / open-source networks. To measure CAUSAL EMERGENCE it defines micro-level state variables, coarse-graining functions, and a tractable measurement framework. Seven falsifiable propositions link CAS theory to software evolution, challenging or extending Lehman's laws where agent-level assumptions fail. If confirmed, the finding 'would demand a radical shift: ecosystem-level monitoring as the primary governance mechanism for AI-native systems.' The title is Anderson's emergence motto - this is the project's central thesis in the software-engineering domain, with a falsifiable measurement program attached (still a position paper: the seven propositions are not yet tested - hence modest confidence). Companion to the large-N empirical result concept_ai_native_software_risk_is_an_ecosystem_property_not_an_agent_property.

nodes.label: Two agents alternately updating from each other under misaligned objectives reach a biased equilibrium - neither hits its target, residual error predictable from the objective gap and prompt geometry; an adversarial agent can converge exactly while holding the other in persistent bias
nodes.description: Convergence dynamics of Agent-to-Agent Interactions with Misaligned objectives (arXiv:2511.08710, VERIFIED via arXiv abstract read run 210). A theoretical / mechanistic framework: each agent is a single-layer transformer with linear self-attention (LSA) trained to implement gradient-descent-like updates on a quadratic in-context regression objective; two such agents alternately update from each other's outputs under potentially misaligned fixed objectives. Results within this simplified setting: (1) misalignment leads to a BIASED EQUILIBRIUM where neither agent reaches its target, with residual errors PREDICTABLE from the objective gap and the prompt-induced geometry; (2) an ADVERSARIAL regime where asymmetric convergence is possible - one agent reaches its objective exactly while inducing persistent bias in the other; (3) an adaptive contrast: a helper agent updating a turn-based objective to implement a Newton-like step for the main agent eliminates the plateau and accelerates convergence. Experiments with trained LSA agents AND black-box GPT-5-mini runs on in-context linear regression are consistent with the theory within this simplified setting. CURRENCY / RECENCY: Nov 2025, ~10 months old relative to the 2026-09 frontier, and a TOY MODEL (linear self-attention, in-context linear regression) - so low confidence as a claim about real multi-agent LLM systems; its value is as one of the few MECHANISTIC (not merely phenomenological) accounts linking prompt geometry + objective misalignment to stability, bias, and robustness, and the GPT-5-mini check keeps it relevant. Relates to MAST's failure taxonomy (a mechanism for some of its modes), the herding result (a mechanism for why votes converge off-target), and emergent_no_equilibrium_convergence (this says misaligned agents DO converge - to a biased fixed point - in a setting simple enough to solve).

nodes.label: Coding agents are evaluated as models but deployed as systems; reliability is a dependency chain across harness / execution state / retrieval / memory / permissions / verification / observability, and a fix at one layer often fails to propagate end-to-end
nodes.description: Engineering Reliable Coding Agents: Evaluating and Operating the System Around the Model (arXiv:2608.13867, VERIFIED via arXiv abstract read run 211; Aug 2026). A monograph-length structured multivocal review synthesising 164 scholarly works, 100 practitioner records, 29 benchmark records, and 17 author-system case records. Core claim: AI coding agents are commonly EVALUATED AS MODELS but DEPLOYED AS SYSTEMS - reliability depends on the harness, execution state, retrieval, memory and state management, permissions, review interfaces, and resource allocation, not only model capability. Across the evidence: many apparent MODEL failures originate elsewhere in the system, and improvements at one layer often FAIL TO PROPAGATE to end-to-end outcomes. Evaluation and operation are treated as a DEPENDENCY CHAIN in which weaknesses in task construction, execution environments, retrieval, state management, verification, or observability can INVALIDATE downstream conclusions. Contributions: a versioned catalog of 206 reliability records (193 gated practices, 56 developed in depth, 13 research leads); an evidence ledger; a framework for dependency and REPAIR ASYMMETRY across the agent lifecycle; measurements and failure cases from operated systems; runnable evaluation and reliability protocols; five reusable agent skills with evidence maps. Honest limits (recorded in the paper): the review is structured not exhaustive, evidence strength varies by topic, results depend on workload and configuration, and it records which search lanes remain unexecuted. Bearing on the project: this is the project's entire thesis - agent quality is a model-harness-system property, per-layer verification matters, task construction can invalidate a held-out score - restated as a large practitioner+academic synthesis, with a 206-record catalog the project's tools/ and docs/ can be checked against. Recency: Aug 2026, current coding-agent generation.

nodes.label: One operational act appears as many incompatible runtime records; deployer-side governance needs a canonical action object binding approval to execution that an independent verifier can reproduce later
nodes.description: CAVA - Canonical Action Verification and Attestation for Runtime Governance of Agentic AI Systems (arXiv:2607.13716, VERIFIED via arXiv abstract read run 212; July 2026). Agentic systems act through heterogeneous runtimes - local coding hooks, SDK tools, browser automation, managed-agent traces, API gateways, workflow engines - so a single operational act (publishing code, changing identity state, moving money, exporting data) is represented by many incompatible runtime records. That makes a basic governance question hard: WHAT action was actually approved, WHAT evidence binds the approval to execution, and can an independent verifier REPRODUCE the same action identity later? CAVA is a runtime-semantics layer that converts heterogeneous agent activity into CANONICAL runtime action objects. It sits BELOW Proof-Carrying Agent Actions (PCAA): PCAA defines the deployer-owned route-review-prove governance process, CAVA defines the stable action object that process governs. It formalizes canonical action identity, semantic pattern detection, approval binding, receipt integrity, runtime-portable projection, and optional attestation substrates. Evaluated on a 96-seed, 384-variant benchmark covering semantic equivalence, semantic separation, WRAPPER BYPASS, false-positive control, approval binding, receipt reproducibility, ATTESTATION TAMPER DETECTION, runtime portability, policy degradation, and Azure deployment drills. Bearing on the project: this is pattern_evidence_carrying_termination (a typed certificate binding a claim to trace evidence) and pattern_four_field_constraint (approval = authority + prerequisite) generalised to the ACTION level, and it is the concrete defence against emergent_authorization_laundering - 'what evidence binds the approval to execution' plus independent-verifier reproducibility is exactly what a laundered 'I was allowed to X' cannot produce. Recency: July 2026, current; a systems formulation with a benchmark, not yet independently replicated.

nodes.label: Runtime-neutral governance centres on a portable action certificate - five checkpoints (pre-action admissibility, action open, assumption capture, approval, outcome closure) - that is externality-aware and uses explicit enforceability classes, not a reviewed/unreviewed bit
nodes.description: Proof-Carrying Agent Actions (PCAA, arXiv:2606.04104, VERIFIED via arXiv abstract read run 213; June 2026). Agent systems execute through runtimes with very different control points (local coding tools, framework SDKs, managed platforms, API gateways, observer-only integrations), so a high-risk action like publishing data externally appears as a shell command in one, a tool call in another, a hosted session transition in a third. PCAA is a runtime-neutral governance model centred on an ACTION CERTIFICATE rather than a vendor-native session record. It organises control around FIVE CHECKPOINTS: pre-action admissibility, action open, assumption capture, approval, outcome closure - bound to a portable action envelope, runtime and approval receipts, and replay-ready proof. Two practical extensions: (1) the certificate is EXTERNALITY-AWARE, carrying boundary facts such as destination visibility and account provenance; (2) approval is described by explicit ENFORCEABILITY CLASSES rather than a single reviewed/unreviewed bit. Studied via a reference implementation in a heterogeneous agent control plane and a disclosure-bounded protocol; on a benchmark expanded from 24 executable seeds to 96 traces across four runtime families, PCAA preserves route quality while exposing distinct failure modes under ablation. PCAA is the layer ABOVE CAVA (concept_governance_needs_a_canonical_action_identity_across_heterogeneous_runtimes): CAVA is the stable action object, PCAA is the route-review-prove process over it. Bearing on the project: the five checkpoints + 'under whose authority / what approval semantics / what evidence after execution' is pattern_four_field_constraint (prerequisite / authority / fallback / consequence) as a runtime protocol; 'externality-aware boundary facts' (destination visibility, account provenance) is exactly what concept_irreversibility_budget needs to price an act; 'enforceability classes not a reviewed/unreviewed bit' directly answers concept_overseer_degradation's finding that permission policies are 20.1pp weaker than per-action review. Recency: June 2026, a systems formulation with a reference implementation, not yet independently replicated.

nodes.label: SEA: confine self-modification to a small steering adapter + versioned harness around a FROZEN base; admit each edit only through an anytime-valid gate emitting an auditable certificate against a fixed error budget; the gate can only SELECT behaviors the base already produces
nodes.description: SEA - Self-Evolving Agents with Anytime-Valid Certificates (arXiv:2607.00871, VERIFIED via arXiv abstract read run 214; July 2026). Premise: self-evolving agents violate the assumption behind most learning-theoretic guarantees - the data, evaluator, components, and hypothesis space are all produced by the policy being updated. SEA's architecture: confine self-modification to a small STEERING ADAPTER and a VERSIONED HARNESS around a FROZEN base model, and admit each modification only through an ANYTIME-VALID gate that emits an AUDITABLE CERTIFICATE against a FIXED ERROR BUDGET. Five loop controllers compose published guarantees. Crucially: because such gates can only SELECT among behaviors the frozen base ALREADY PRODUCES, five verifier-in-the-loop mechanisms - best-of-N, micro-step search, self-authored reproduction oracles, search-layer control, self-repair - supply the dense, GRADER-FREE signal the gates require, computed from the issue text alone. Evaluation: a 52-instance SWE-bench Verified subset across four base models. BASE CAPABILITY IS THE DOMINANT, CONFOUND-FREE EFFECT; a deliberate no-op-composite control isolates the suite's contribution at +4 and +5 on two strong base models (GLM 5.2 24->28; GPT 29->34), with event logs confirming the mechanisms fire and prevent regressions. Honest limits (stated): single-run on expensive evaluations; run-to-run variance and per-task algorithm mix are future work. Bearing on the project: this is the project's ENTIRE STANCE, published - emergence-first (the gate only selects behaviors the frozen base already produces, no weight training), harness-level self-improvement (steering adapter + versioned harness), verifier-gated promotion with an auditable certificate, a fixed error budget (concept_irreversibility_budget), grader-free dense signal from the task text (concept_inference_time_scaling_of_verification). It is the fifth independent arrival at the plan (after ASG-SI, Self-Harness, SEAL, Falsifiable Release Gates) and the one that matches the no-training fork most exactly. Recency: July 2026, current base models.

nodes.label: Orchestration failures need cascade-radius + per-failure-mode recovery metrics, not task accuracy; three recovery tiers across five MAST modes (tool faults ~1.0, ambiguous delegation ~0.30, latent/semantic ~0.0), stable across models; blind retry hides latent faults
nodes.description: OrchestraBench: Evaluating Multi-Agent Orchestration Failure Modes, Recovery, and Decomposition Quality (arXiv:2608.05263, VERIFIED via arXiv abstract read run 216; Aug 2026). Multi-agent orchestration benchmarks report task accuracy without diagnosing WHY a pipeline failed, WHERE a cascade began, or WHICH routing decision caused the breakdown. OrchestraBench is a controlled, seed-reproducible FAILURE-INJECTION harness over templated enterprise workflows, with two primary metrics: CASCADE RADIUS and PER-FAILURE-MODE RECOVERY. Findings: (1) on a 26-case gold diagnostic a keyword/flag router scores 0% on adversarial cases with misleading or missing surface flags while an intent-reasoning model router scores 100% (matches the oracle); (2) controlled mechanism probes with a REAL Claude agent over a verifiable arithmetic dependency chain reveal THREE FAILURE-HANDLING TIERS across five MAST modes - tool faults recover fully (1.0), ambiguous delegation partially (0.30), and three latent or semantic modes NEVER recover (0.0); this ordering PERSISTS when the chain is reframed as a loan-approval workflow and across Sonnet, Opus, and Haiku (absolute rates shift with context); (3) BLIND RETRY reproduces latent faults and increases time to detection - detection and attribution are necessary for containment; (4) cascade radius grows with pipeline depth (mean 0.9 -> 4.7 across depths 3-7); (5) a trusted-state repair ablation shows apparent containment gains come primarily from the trusted-state signal, not autonomous detection. Honest scoping (stated): controlled-chain mechanism probes, not domain-workload claims. Bearing on the project: this operationalises concept_mast_multi_agent_failure_taxonomy with recovery rates, and 'detection and attribution are necessary for containment' + 'where a cascade began' is exactly the job of artifact_phase0_trace_substrate + tools/topology_recover.py. Recency: Aug 2026, tested on the current Claude model family.

nodes.label: In some domains (incident response) multi-agent orchestration is not a performance optimisation but a production-readiness requirement: 100% vs 1.7% actionable, zero quality variance across 348 trials
nodes.description: Multi-Agent LLM Orchestration Achieves Deterministic, High-Quality Decision Support for Incident Response (arXiv:2511.15755, VERIFIED via arXiv abstract read run 217). A reproducible containerised framework (MyAntFarm.ai). Across 348 controlled trials comparing a single-agent copilot vs a multi-agent system on identical incident scenarios: multi-agent achieves a 100% ACTIONABLE recommendation rate vs 1.7% for single-agent (an 80x improvement in action specificity, 140x in solution correctness), and multi-agent systems exhibit ZERO quality variance across all trials, enabling production SLA commitments impossible with inconsistent single-agent outputs. Both architectures have similar comprehension latency (~40s), so the architectural value is deterministic quality, not speed. Introduces Decision Quality (DQ) - validity + specificity + correctness. Framing: 'reframe multi-agent orchestration from a performance optimization to a production-readiness requirement for LLM-based incident response.' CURRENCY / CONFIDENCE NOTE: Nov 2025, a SINGLE domain (incident response), and the framing is promotional (a named product, 80x/140x headline multipliers); folded at confidence 0.5 as a domain-specific counterweight, not a general claim. Its value: it is a concrete domain where multi-agent DECISIVELY beats single-agent, which stands in tension with concept_mast_multi_agent_failure_taxonomy's 'MAS gains often minimal' and with 'Beyond the Strongest' discarding ~8 points of recoverable correctness - the resolution is that the win is task-structure dependent (incident response = decompose-diagnose-recommend, where specialised roles and a deterministic synthesis genuinely help).

nodes.label: Multi-agent orchestration helps when the task decomposes into independently-verifiable subtasks recombined by a deterministic synthesis step; it hurts when agents vote, share partial reasoning, or recombine by consensus
nodes.description: A synthesis node (run 218, no new citation) resolving the multi-agent tension the graph has accumulated. The conflicting evidence: concept_mast_multi_agent_failure_taxonomy ('MAS gains often minimal', 14 failure modes); 'Beyond the Strongest' (orchestration on GPQA-Diamond reached 87.4% while at least one agent was right in 95.5% - discards ~8 points of individually-recoverable correctness, via concept_orchestration_failure_is_diagnosable_by_cascade_radius_and_per_mode_recovery); concept_orchestration_can_beat_the_strongest_model_but_showing_votes_causes_herding (it CAN beat the strongest model, but only if authorship and vote tallies are hidden); concept_multi_agent_orchestration_wins_decisively_in_some_domains_incident_response (100% vs 1.7% actionable, zero variance, in one domain); concept_epistemic_sybil_collapse (multiplying agents on SHARED evidence collapses aggregate confidence). The resolving criterion: multi-agent pays off when (a) the task DECOMPOSES into subtasks each with an independent, checkable success condition, (b) the subtask outputs are recombined by a DETERMINISTIC synthesis step (a computed merge, a schema fill, a typed aggregation) rather than by a vote or a consensus discussion, and (c) the agents work from DISJOINT evidence / context slices (pattern_structural_decoupling), not a shared pool. It hurts when agents see each other's partial reasoning (herding), vote (herding + epistemic Sybil collapse), or recompose by consensus (latent/semantic failure modes never recover, OrchestraBench). Incident response fits (a)+(b)+(c) - decompose / diagnose / recommend with specialised roles and a deterministic recommendation synthesis; open-ended reasoning benchmarks (GPQA) fit none, which is why orchestration discards recoverable correctness there. This is a testable claim: the project's Phase 0 trace substrate + topology_recover.py can measure (a)/(b)/(c) on any real swarm trace and predict whether the orchestration helped. RIG (run 221): tools/probe_orchestration_value.py operationalises the three conditions as sim knobs; dry-run verdict CONFIRMS - a&b&c gives +0.52 vs single and is strictly the best of the 8 combos, every combo missing one condition is <=+0.20, vote-synthesis and shared-pool combos never exceed +0.15. artifact_probe_orchestration_value_rig.

nodes.label: The when-does-multi-agent-help criterion as a runnable rig - verdict: CONFIRMS (helps only with verifiable subtasks + deterministic synthesis + disjoint evidence)
nodes.description: tools/probe_orchestration_value.py, run 221 (operationalises the run-218 synthesis concept_multi_agent_helps_when_subtasks_are_verifiable_and_synthesis_is_deterministic). Controlled sim: a task of K=8 subtasks, SINGLE (one agent, growing accumulation penalty) vs MULTI (K fresh agents + a synthesis step) with three binary knobs on MULTI - (a) verifiable: each subtask output is checked and retried once; (b) deterministic: synthesis is a computed merge, else a vote that adds BASE_HERD=0.50 + per-disagreement herding; (c) disjoint: subtask errors independent, else a shared evidence pool with a poisoned fact that verification CANNOT fix (the retry agent re-reads the same pool - epistemic Sybil collapse). Dry-run (4000 trials/combo): SINGLE ~0.46; MULTI with a&b&c +0.52 delta and strictly the best of the 8 combos; every combo missing any one of the three is <=+0.20 (best non-full = a0b1c1 at +0.20 - deterministic+disjoint without verification gives a modest benefit; verification makes it decisive); vote-synthesis combos and shared-pool combos never exceed +0.15. Verdict CONFIRMS the criterion at these params. Stub: _subtask_ok / _synthesis_ok (swap for real agent runs); a Phase 6 probe once a real multi-agent harness exists. Emits a swarm-layer trace that validates. SENSITIVITY (run 249): a 16-cell grid (BASE_HERD x POISON_DRAG, 2500 trials/cell) - the CONFIRMS verdict's shape is parameter-robust (a1b1c1 always +0.526 and strictly best; best partial always +0.192; a1b1c1/a0b1c1 are insensitive to both knobs by construction). One sub-check is parameter-sensitive: 'no vote-synthesis config strongly helps' needs BASE_HERD >= ~0.42 (the default 0.50 has margin); below the flip a vote is weakly helpful, never as good as a deterministic merge. See docs/probe_orchestration_value.md. FLOCK ARM (run 273): a third architecture with NO synthesiser - K agents each append one subtask result to a shared store, each reads a bounded neighbourhood (3) of prior contributions and can be dragged by a wrong one (FLOCK_CONTAGION=0.45), plus a small no-final-review penalty (0.03); the store itself is the output, passing at >=95% subtasks right. Result (verifiable + disjoint): flock helps +0.31 vs SINGLE - BELOW the perfect deterministic-synthesis ceiling (+0.52) but far ABOVE any vote-synthesis MULTI, and a shared evidence pool still kills it (+0.04). So run-218 condition (b) is not strictly 'deterministic synthesis' - it is 'deterministic synthesis OR bounded-neighbourhood stigmergic accretion'; conditions (a) verifiable and (c) disjoint still bind. 5 new selftest checks (14 total in the rig).

nodes.label: Source-code anatomy of 11 production coding harnesses: seven canonical subsystems, 29 patterns; no runtime imports an agentic framework or uses vector code-retrieval; SKILL.md leads MCP (9/11 vs 8/11); behavioural policy migrating from prompt prose to configuration; the coding harness turned from tool to platform in H1 2026
nodes.description: Harness Engineering: Anatomy, Architecture, and Evolution of Coding Agents - A Source-Code Study of Eleven Systems (arXiv:2609.00006, VERIFIED via arXiv abstract read run 222; July 2026). The most comprehensive empirical foundation to date for 'harness engineering' (named as a discipline in early 2026): a source-code anatomy of ELEVEN production coding harnesses - Claude Code, Codex CLI, Gemini CLI, Mistral Vibe, OpenHands, Aider, Mini-SWE-Agent, Hermes, Pi, OpenCode, OpenClaw - plus Omnigent, 'the first meta-harness', as a contrast point. Defines a harness (loop + tools + context management + safety controls + orchestration + extension surfaces), maps its SEVEN canonical subsystems with the minimal and maximal implementation of each, and dissects all eleven along those subsystems. Yields 13 cross-cutting observations and a catalog of 29 recurring design patterns. Headline findings, across ~4 MILLION lines of Python / TypeScript / Rust and surviving a threefold corpus expansion: (1) NO agent runtime imports a general-purpose agentic framework; (2) NONE retrieves code with vector embeddings - the field runs on hand-rolled async loops and DETERMINISTIC retrieval; (3) SKILL.md skills lead MCP in adoption (9/11 vs 8/11); (4) ACP ships in six systems with a new third role: harness hosting. A controlled LONGITUDINAL sample (the original eight systems re-pinned and source-diffed across one quarter) shows 'convergence becoming imitation' and 'behavioral policy migrating from prompt prose to configuration'. Thesis: in the first half of 2026 the coding harness completed a turn from tool to platform. Closes with 18 design recommendations and a 90-line minimum-viable-harness scaffold. Bearing on the project: this is direct empirical validation of the project's build choices - pure stdlib / no framework (finding 1), substring / deterministic retrieval in experience_bank (finding 2), SKILL.md for the scheduled loop (finding 3), and context/loop_policy as a CONFIG component not prose (the prose-to-configuration migration). The seven canonical subsystems are the concept_bottleneck_is_the_model_harness_coupling decomposition, empirically grounded. Omnigent the meta-harness is approach_self_improving_harness shipped by someone else. Recency: July 2026, current harness generation, and it names Hermes (the owner's own agent).

nodes.label: Self-evolving coding agents, taxonomised by target of evolution (framework / memory / skills+tools / components / workflow+topology / environment+context); executable feedback is the code-specific signal; shared challenges: feedback reliability, benchmark overfitting, reversibility, complexity, safety, cost, generalization
nodes.description: Self-Evolving Coding Agents (survey, arXiv:2608.03392, VERIFIED via arXiv abstract read run 223; Aug 2026). A structured synthesis of self-evolving CODING agents - distinguished from conventional coding agents and from general self-evolving agents. Taxonomy centred on the TARGETS OF EVOLUTION: framework, memory, skills and tools, components, workflow and topology, environment and context - i.e. the agent persistently updates one of these from prior coding interactions. Two orthogonal perspectives: WHEN evolution occurs, and WHICH code-specific signals drive it. The domain-specific point: executable feedback, repository-level context, and coding trajectories make software engineering a NATURAL domain for agent self-evolution (dense verifiable signal) - but the same features introduce challenges: FEEDBACK RELIABILITY, BENCHMARK OVERFITTING, REVERSIBILITY, system complexity, safety, cost, and generalization. Bearing on the project: this is concept_what_when_how_where_to_evolve (the general self-evolving-agents taxonomy) specialised to code, and its seven-item challenge list is the project's own worry list - feedback reliability + benchmark overfitting are the acceptor cluster (SEAL / PACE / Who Grades the Grader / search-contamination), reversibility is pattern_recoverability_constrained_evolution, safety is what_would_make_this_wrong.md. 'Executable feedback is the dense code-specific signal' is the same argument as concept_horizon_gap_outcome_signals_decay (the field manufactures denser step-level signal). Recency: Aug 2026, a survey so it lags primary work by ~1-2 quarters.

nodes.label: SHAPER: train-free embodied adaptation - a frozen model evolves its own reusable skills + context-code harness through target-environment rollouts, serving as BOTH planner and optimizer; a practical route when training is expensive, unavailable, or undesirable
nodes.description: SHAPER - Self-evolving framework for train-free embodied adaptation (arXiv:2608.11350, VERIFIED via arXiv abstract read run 224; Aug 2026). Embodied agents are systems around a foundation model, where performance depends on the skills, context, action interfaces, and execution harness around the model - not only weights. SFT and RL adapt agents but need data, rewards, and training runs; train-free code-centric approaches often need programmable robot APIs unavailable in FIXED-INTERFACE settings. SHAPER keeps model parameters FROZEN and improves the non-parametric agent system by evolving REUSABLE SKILLS and a CONTEXT-CODE HARNESS through target-environment rollouts. The same frozen model serves as BOTH planner AND optimizer - it refines its own external skills and harness without parameter updates. Evaluated on VLABench and ESI-Bench (different low-level action interfaces), beating pure execution, SFT, and test-time-scaling baselines (verifier-free selection, voting). Bearing on the project: the same-frozen-model-as-planner-and-optimizer is EXACTLY the project's loop structure - Claude proposes edits to its own harness with no weight training - now demonstrated in the embodied domain, where fixed action interfaces make it the only viable route. Extends the frozen-base thread (SEA, Self-Harness) beyond coding into robotics; 'context-code harness' is concept_ace_context_evolution_self_improvement's context playbook plus executable glue. Recency: Aug 2026; one framework, two embodied benchmarks - modest confidence.

nodes.label: PCN-Rec: separate natural-language reasoning from deterministic enforcement - two agents negotiate + a mediator emits a JSON certificate + a deterministic verifier recomputes every constraint and accepts only verifier-checked certificates, with constrained-greedy repair on failure
nodes.description: PCN-Rec - Agentic Proof-Carrying Negotiation for Reliable Governance-Constrained Recommendation (arXiv:2601.09771, VERIFIED via arXiv abstract read run 227; Jan 2026). LLM recommenders generate compelling lists but struggle to reliably satisfy governance constraints (minimum long-tail exposure, diversity). PCN-Rec is a pipeline that SEPARATES natural-language reasoning from DETERMINISTIC ENFORCEMENT: a base recommender (MF/CF) produces a candidate window of size W; two agents negotiate it - a User Advocate optimising relevance, a Policy Agent enforcing constraints; a mediator LLM synthesises a top-N slate PLUS a structured JSON CERTIFICATE describing the claimed constraint satisfaction; a DETERMINISTIC VERIFIER recomputes ALL constraints from the slate and accepts ONLY verifier-checked certificates; on failure a deterministic constrained-greedy REPAIR produces a compliant slate for re-verification, yielding an AUDITABLE TRACE. On MovieLens-100K: 98.55% pass rate on feasible users (n=551, W=80) vs a one-shot single-LLM baseline without verification/repair, preserving utility (0.021 absolute NDCG@10 drop, 0.403 vs 0.424; p<0.05). Bearing on the project: a clean small-scale instance of pattern_grounded_acceptance_only + pattern_evidence_carrying_termination - the LLM proposes and explains, a deterministic check is the authority, and a repair loop keeps the trace auditable. The two-agents-plus-deterministic-mediator structure is exactly the run-218 criterion (verifiable subtasks + DETERMINISTIC synthesis) applied to a governed recommendation task. Recency/currency: Jan 2026, one benchmark (MovieLens-100K), recommendation domain - modest confidence; the architecture is domain-general. IMPLEMENTED (run 232, synthetic-task path): improvement_loop.deterministic_repair - on a rejected compaction-policy proposal, a bounded constrained fix pins the risk-protected classes without widening the blast radius, then re-verifies; a passing repair is promoted flagged verdict['repaired']=True. Cannot touch the holdout or risk measure, so it can only make a proposal more conservative.

nodes.label: Lifecycle reasoning in dynamic harnesses (which components a change affects, state after a teardown order, conditions holding under all/some orders) degrades as relevant interactions grow, costs ~3000 reasoning tokens/question, and is fully replaced by an independent finite reference semantics on controlled instances
nodes.description: CordisBench (arXiv:2609.01600, VERIFIED via arXiv abstract read run 228; Sept 2026). Dynamic agent harnesses let a model change the software that shapes its own execution - and a local plugin change propagates through dependencies and cleanup, a new REASONING BURDEN. CordisBench is a 1,200-question benchmark of that lifecycle reasoning: identify affected components, predict state after a specified teardown ORDER, determine which conditions hold under ALL or SOME orders, choose reconfigurations that succeed when executed. It pairs a controlled formal setting with programs executed against Cordis, a runtime that manages component dependencies and cleanup, with deterministic task-specific scoring. Findings: three efficiency-oriented models at low reasoning effort with 2-32 relevant interactions - models usually handle SMALL systems well but GROW LESS RELIABLE as more interactions become relevant, especially predicting final state and reasoning across teardown orders; additional inference effort recovers marked gains for some; the cost is nontrivial (GPT-5.6 Luna ~3,000 reasoning tokens/question at medium effort on the 16-interaction subset). CRUCIALLY: for these controlled instances the cost is AVOIDABLE - an independent finite REFERENCE SEMANTICS agrees with Cordis execution on every observation and action outcome used for scoring across all 528 executable questions. Bearing on the project: the self-improving loop modifies its own harness components (harness_registry version chains, context/loop_policy, skill induction/retirement); reasoning about the downstream effects of a component change is exactly this lifecycle reasoning, and CordisBench says an LLM's version of it is (a) unreliable at scale and (b) fully replaceable by a deterministic checker on controlled cases - a direct argument for the project's deterministic-where-possible stance (exec_guard, deterministic validate, tampering_flags, paired_eprocess). Recency: Sept 2026, current reasoning models.

nodes.label: Self-improvement should be live, not post-hoc: a supervisor-worker harness where a separate supervisor redirects/aborts the active worker mid-run and distils failure modes into reusable skills during execution; ranks first in 5/6 configs, cuts mean output tokens ~45%
nodes.description: PILOT in the Loop: Live Self-Improvement for Long-Horizon Agents (arXiv:2608.26530, VERIFIED via arXiv abstract read run 230; Aug 2026). Most self-improvement methods process a run's experience only AFTER execution ends, so they cannot redirect the active run or immediately apply and validate lessons from it. PILOT argues self-improvement should be LIVE - using emerging experience both to redirect the active run and to update the persistent harness. Existing architectures do not support this: single-agent self-correction mixes execution and assessment in one context; subagent delegation separates execution but cannot redirect an active subagent. PILOT is a SUPERVISOR-WORKER harness with two coupled mechanisms: (1) LIVE STEERING - a separate supervisor redirects or ABORTS the active worker during execution; (2) LIVE SELF-EVOLUTION - distils procedures and failure modes revealed during execution into reusable skills and memory. Across two FROZEN backbones and three benchmarks, PILOT ranks first in 5 of 6 configs; on Terminal-Bench 2.0 it beats counterpart harnesses by up to 9.8pp; in the self-improvement setting +14.6 (GLM-5.1) / +12.4 (Kimi-K2.6). Mean output tokens FALL 42.9% / 47.4%; successful evaluations per million output tokens RISE 110.3% / 134.0%. Bearing on the project: the project's three-loop is between-run (concept_self_harness_validates_the_three_loop) - observe-trace -> minimal proposal -> held-out regression, once per run. PILOT says the highest-value version runs the supervisor DURING the run, aborting a doomed worker rather than scoring it afterward. 'Abort the active worker' is a live recoverability mechanism; the token-efficiency numbers make the case that a supervisor watching a worker is cheaper than a long single context. Frozen-backbone, so it is in the emergence-first / no-training fork. Recency: Aug 2026, current frozen backbones (GLM-5.1, Kimi-K2.6).

nodes.label: JIT-Agent: a TRAINED harness-generator model synthesizes task-adaptive harnesses on the fly for off-the-shelf LLMs under a fixed four-module protocol; makes weaker models beat stronger ones (+9-20pp); harness intelligence is trainable, transferable, compounding, orthogonal to model scaling
nodes.description: JIT-Agent: Scaling Harness Intelligence via Just-in-Time Harness Evolution (arXiv:2608.25593, VERIFIED via arXiv abstract read run 231; Aug 2026). Agent capability is not the model alone - the harness (memory management, planning strategy, action protocol, tool/skill orchestration) can DOMINATE the foundation model's contribution. Yet harness design is manual, task-specific, unscalable. JIT-Agent is a HARNESS INTELLIGENCE MODEL - a model TRAINED to synthesize task-adaptive agent harnesses on the fly for arbitrary off-the-shelf agentic LLMs. It formalizes the harness as a composable, machine-generatable artifact governed by a FIXED FOUR-MODULE PROTOCOL, and is trained to (a) customize harnesses per task, (b) REPAIR harnesses for stable and reliable execution, (c) self-evolve by distilling performance signals from an expanding ARCHIVE of prior harness configurations. Results: DeepSeek-V4-Flash + JIT-Agent surpasses GPT-5.6 on DeepSearchQA (+9.1) and OdysseyBench (+4.3); the already-strong GLM-5.2 gains up to +20.2; JIT-Agent-generated harnesses are performance-competitive with mature runtimes (OpenCode, Claude Code) and consistently improve DeepSeek V4 / Mimo-V2.5 / Qwen3.6 families. 'The first model purpose-built for just-in-time harness generation, establishing harness intelligence as a TRAINABLE, TRANSFERABLE, and COMPOUNDING dimension of agent capability ORTHOGONAL to model scaling.' Bearing on the project: this is a genuine TENSION with the emergence-first / no-weight-training fork - JIT-Agent trains a dedicated harness-generator model and shows it compounds, an alternative to elicitation-only harness improvement. But it is also the strongest published statement of concept_capability_is_a_model_harness_config_property (a weaker model + a good harness beats a stronger model), and its fixed four-module protocol echoes pattern_four_field_constraint. Recorded as a challenges edge to approach_emergence_first. Recency: Aug 2026, current model families.

nodes.label: AHE: component + experience + decision observability turn every harness edit into a falsifiable contract; 10 iterations 69.7->77.0% on Terminal-Bench 2 (beating the human harness); the frozen harness transfers cross-family +5-10pp; the gain is in tools/middleware/memory NOT the system prompt - factual structure transfers, prose strategy doesn't
nodes.description: Agentic Harness Engineering (AHE, arXiv:2604.25850, VERIFIED via arXiv abstract read run 233; April 2026 - the ANCHOR paper of the harness-evolution subfield, opened directly to remove the 'indexed, NOT independently opened' caveat on concept_harness_evolution_subfield). Automating harness engineering faces three challenges: a heterogeneous action space across editable components, voluminous trajectories that bury signal, and edits whose effect is hard to attribute. AHE is a closed loop with three MATCHED OBSERVABILITY PILLARS: (1) COMPONENT observability - every editable component gets a file-level representation so the action space is explicit and REVERTIBLE; (2) EXPERIENCE observability - millions of raw trajectory tokens distilled into a layered, drill-down evidence corpus an evolving agent can consume; (3) DECISION observability - every edit paired with a self-declared PREDICTION, later verified against the next round's task-level outcomes. Together these turn every edit into a FALSIFIABLE CONTRACT so evolution proceeds without collapsing into trial-and-error. Empirically: 10 iterations lift Terminal-Bench 2 pass@1 69.7% -> 77.0%, surpassing the human-designed Codex-CLI (71.9%) and self-evolving baselines ACE and TF-GRPO. THE FROZEN HARNESS TRANSFERS without re-evolution: SWE-bench-verified aggregate success at 12% FEWER tokens than the seed; +5.1 to +10.1pp CROSS-FAMILY gains across three alternate model families - so the evolved components encode GENERAL engineering experience, not benchmark tuning. Ablations LOCALIZE the gain to TOOLS, MIDDLEWARE, and LONG-TERM MEMORY rather than the system prompt: FACTUAL HARNESS STRUCTURE TRANSFERS WHILE PROSE-LEVEL STRATEGY DOES NOT. Bearing on the project: the three pillars are the project's Phase 1 (harness_registry, file-level revertible components), Phase 2 (experience_bank + trace_substrate), and Phase 3 (prediction per edit in loop_proposer / verify_loop_edit) - AHE is the project's build, published and measured. The prose-doesn't-transfer ablation is direct support for context/loop_policy being config and for concentrating self-improvement on tools/memory not prompts. Recency: April 2026, older than the 30-day window - currency note: current-generation baselines (Codex-CLI, ACE) but pre-dates GPT-5.6 / GLM-5.2; the falsifiable-contract mechanism and the structure-vs-prose ablation are model-agnostic.

nodes.label: WHALE: agent performance depends jointly on weights and harness; optimizing either alone leaves the system bottlenecked by its frozen counterpart; alternating weight/harness updates beats weight-only, harness-only, and Fast-Slow by 4.15-24.38pp on small (Qwen3.5-2B/4B) agents
nodes.description: WHALE - Weight-Harness Alternating LEarning (arXiv:2609.00196, VERIFIED via arXiv abstract read run 236; Aug 2026). Agent performance depends JOINTLY on model parameters and the executable harness code that manages context and control flow. Optimizing EITHER component in isolation leaves the system BOTTLENECKED BY ITS FROZEN COUNTERPART: weight updates change which harness is effective, while harness updates change which model capabilities are exposed. Existing joint-adaptation methods optimize weights and textual PROMPTS but leave the broader harness fixed. WHALE alternates two phases: update the model under the current harness (online rejection-sampling fine-tuning), then search for a better harness under the updated model (Meta-Harness); a fixed-phase or adaptive-patience rule decides when to switch. Qwen3.5-2B/4B agents across search-QA, math reasoning, and chess puzzles: WHALE outperforms weight-only, harness-only, and Fast-Slow Training by 4.15-24.38pp in best mean@8 accuracy. EITHER component can be the bottleneck: harness search matches peak weight-only accuracy with FAR FEWER rollouts in SearchQA, but improves math accuracy ONLY AFTER a weight update. Small interleaved updates beat stagewise weight-then-harness in accuracy and rollout cost. Bearing on the project: this is the SHARPEST empirical challenge to the emergence-first / no-weight-training fork - and it is measured on SMALL models (the project's regime). It does not say the harness doesn't matter (harness-only wins SearchQA cheaply); it says harness-only hits a ceiling the frozen model sets, and on some tasks (math) you cannot cross it without a weight update. The project's counter-position: interpretability and the absence of training infra are deliberate constraints, and many target tasks (research direction-setting, graph engineering) are elicitation-shaped not weight-shaped - but WHALE makes 'harness-only is enough' a bet with a measured cost on the tasks where it is not. Recency: Aug 2026, current small models; code released.

nodes.label: ASPIRE: given only a vague natural-language goal (hidden eval), agents spend search on goal interpretation, complete training/harness loops but weight gains are sparse and unstable, the best evolved harness stays below an engineered reference, and continued search erases earlier gains
nodes.description: ASPIRE: Can Models Self-Evolve from Vague Goals? (arXiv:2608.31111, VERIFIED via arXiv abstract read run 238; Aug 2026). Existing LLM self-evolution work begins with human-specified tasks and metrics, reducing self-evolution to optimising an explicit objective rather than DECIDING WHAT AND HOW TO LEARN. ASPIRE is a benchmark for VAGUE-GOAL-DRIVEN self-evolution: it provides only a natural-language capability goal ('become better at X') while downstream evaluation tasks stay HIDDEN. The agent must operationalise the goal - choose data and update methods, construct training and validation signals, decide when to evaluate. It supports both model-weight AND agent-harness evolution in one interactive environment; evaluation is a hidden, expert-authored 520-item set across six goals. Findings: (1) vague goals REDIRECT SEARCH EFFORT toward goal interpretation; (2) agents routinely complete training and harness-editing loops, but WEIGHT-LEVEL GAINS REMAIN SPARSE AND UNSTABLE, and the strongest evolved harness REMAINS BELOW the engineered Qwen-Agent reference; (3) agents often TRAIN ON MISMATCHED DATA and TRUST NARROW SELF-EVALUATIONS, so local gains fail to transfer to hidden evaluation; (4) CONTINUED SEARCH AND TRAINING CAN ERASE EARLIER IMPROVEMENTS. Bearing on the project: the project's own top-level structure is a vague goal - the human sets the research direction ('keep researching until I say stop'), the loop operationalises it. ASPIRE measures exactly this and finds it hard: agents over-invest in interpreting the goal, over-trust their own narrow checks, and regress. This is why the project keeps the human at research-direction-setting (concept_self_improvement_strength_tracks_the_verification_hierarchy's top-of-hierarchy bottleneck), why the held-out set is frozen and exogenous, and why the IDLE-STATE RULE exists (to stop the loop erasing its own gains with low-value churn). A BOTH-SIDES caution: neither harness-only nor weight evolution from a vague goal beats an engineered reference. Recency: Aug 2026, current models.

nodes.label: HELIX: harness, model, and data form a feedback system - harness evolution improves fixed-model execution AND produces matched success/regression/near-miss records as training data; a source-traceable substrate (typed ports/atoms/recipes/shells/policies); a candidate portfolio exposes 58% more verified coverage via complementary sibling behaviour
nodes.description: HELIX: Model-Harness Co-evolution for Recursive Self-Improvement (arXiv:2608.13951, VERIFIED via arXiv abstract read run 239; Aug 2026). An interactive agent acts through a runtime harness that mediates context, tools, control flow, and stopping - the harness shapes both what a model can accomplish AND the trajectories from which it learns. This coupling motivates model-harness CO-EVOLUTION: build harnesses for a fixed model, update the model from verified sibling trajectories, rebuild the harnesses as capabilities change. Realising the loop needs a controlled way to evolve harnesses while PRESERVING INTERVENTION IDENTITY AND EFFECT. HELIX is a SOURCE-TRACEABLE SUBSTRATE that decomposes agent systems into typed PORTS, reusable ATOMS, RECIPES, PRODUCT SHELLS, and RUNTIME POLICIES - interventions explicit and auditable, trajectories / test outcomes / provenance retained. Harness evolution serves two linked roles: improving fixed-model execution, AND producing matched successes / regressions / near misses / alternatives as DATA for the next model update. One evolution round on code repair: a 65-candidate portfolio finds a fixed harness improving task coverage 4.0% over Pi, while the FULL PORTFOLIO exposes up to 58.0% MORE verified coverage through COMPLEMENTARY SIBLING BEHAVIOUR; a 200-slot sibling slice yields 438 verified SFT / critic / filter / preference records. Bearing on the project: the typed-component decomposition (ports/atoms/recipes/shells/policies) is a more granular harness_registry; 'source-traceable, provenance retained' is Phase 0-1; the two-roles framing adds one the project does not use - harness evolution as a TRAINING-DATA GENERATOR (the project stops at improving execution, no weight update). The 58% complementary-sibling coverage is a portfolio/diversity result: multiple harness variants catch complementary cases, which is pattern_structural_decoupling and the run-218 multi-agent criterion at the harness-variant level. Third data point (with WHALE, JIT-Agent) that model-harness coupling rewards co-evolution - but HELIX's harness-only number (+4% over Pi) also holds up the harness-matters half. Recency: Aug 2026.

nodes.label: In LLM-supported research ideation, perceived creativity support does NOT rise linearly with control, human effort shifts from ideating to VERIFYING ideas, and ownership becomes a negotiated human-AI outcome; design for researcher empowerment, not for operating an automated process
nodes.description: Who Owns Creativity and Who Does the Work? Trade-offs in LLM-Supported Research Ideation (arXiv:2601.12152, VERIFIED via arXiv abstract read run 240; Jan 2026). SOURCE: surfaced in the owner's Perplexity deep-research 'Improving Agent Creativity Diversity' (knowledge/notes/2026-09-04-creativity-diversity-mitigation.md on origin/main, 24-50 web searches) - cross-checked and folded here. A mixed-methods study with 54 researchers using an agentic research-ideation system with three roles (Ideator / Writer / Evaluator) across three control levels (Low / Medium / Intensive). Three findings: (1) perceived creativity support does NOT simply increase linearly with greater control - there is a sweet spot, and Intensive control can reduce the felt support; (2) human effort SHIFTS from ideating to VERIFYING ideas; (3) ownership becomes a NEGOTIATED outcome between human and AI. Design implication: emphasise researcher EMPOWERMENT and a sense of ownership over strong ideas, rather than reducing researchers to operating an automated AI-driven process. Bearing on the project: finding (2) is direct empirical corroboration of concept_research_lifecycle_split ('agents do the engineering of research, not the judgement') - with real researchers, the human's job becomes verification. Finding (1) is a nuance on the human-in-the-loop design: more human control is not monotonically better, which bears on the gate design and on where the direction-setting / verification boundary sits. This project is itself an instance - a human sets a standing research direction and the loop operationalises it; ASPIRE (run 238) is the automated-agent version of the same measurement, this is the human-in-the-loop version. Recency/currency: Jan 2026, an HCI study (54 participants) - modest confidence; the findings are about human-AI collaboration structure, not model capability, so they age slowly.

nodes.label: Human knowledge capture for agents: agents don't reliably recognise what's worth recording, so capture must be a platform-level part of the workflow (with contributor approval + risk gating); tacit expertise is grown through structured conversation and periodically crystallised into typed reusable knowledge units
nodes.description: A cluster from the owner's Perplexity deep-research 'Human Knowledge Capture & Creative Work Automation' (knowledge/notes/2026-09-04-human-knowledge-creative-automation.md on origin/main, 50 web searches), cross-checked and folded here. Three papers converge: (1) SHARED ORGANIZATIONAL MEMORY FOR ENTERPRISE CODING AGENTS (arXiv:2608.00122, VERIFIED, Jul 2026, a production deployment) - existing knowledge interfaces 'depend on agents RECOGNISING and explicitly recording lessons worth reusing, disconnecting capture from the coding workflow and leaving development experience repeatedly rediscovered'. Fix: make capture a PLATFORM-LEVEL part of the work - collect task-adjacent experience WITH CONTRIBUTOR APPROVAL, curate into reusable question-answer memories, GATE obvious security and privacy risks, retrieve for future agents. Effects still under evaluation. (2) NURTURE-FIRST AGENT DEVELOPMENT (arXiv:2603.10808, VERIFIED, Mar 2026) - domain expertise is substantially TACIT, deeply personal, and continuously evolving, which breaks the code-first / prompt-first assumption that agent construction is a discrete phase before deployment. NFD: initialise with minimal scaffolding, grow through structured CONVERSATIONAL interaction with domain practitioners; the Knowledge Crystallization Cycle periodically consolidates fragmented dialogue knowledge into structured reusable assets; a three-layer architecture. (3) KNOWLEDGE ACTIVATION / ATOMIC KNOWLEDGE UNITS (arXiv:2603.14805, from the dossier; NOT independently opened) - Codification -> Compression -> Injection -> AKUs with a typed schema (intent, procedure, tools, metadata, governance, continuations, validators); the agent internalises an AKU via injection and 'ephemeral internalization' on task success. Bearing on the project: this CHALLENGES the Phase 2 experience_bank's implicit assumption - the bank condenses from traces, but Shared Org Memory says the agent will not reliably have RECORDED the lesson in the first place (an instance of emergent_recognition_execution_gap). Two fixes the project does not have: (a) capture as an automatic platform step, not agent-initiated; (b) an approval + risk-gate on every write (which is also the memory-poisoning defense). The AKU typed schema is a more governed version of a skill_induction skill. Recency: mixed (Mar-Jul 2026), one production deployment - modest confidence.

nodes.label: 100+ agentic job postings (Aug-Sep 2026, ~1,365 aggregate): harness engineering is a distinct hired discipline separate from model training; self-improving loops (reflection/critique/self-debug) are table stakes in 40%+ of roles; eval rigs + CI gates are near-universal; DeepSeek hires explicitly for model-harness co-evolution ('DeepSeek CodeHarness' vs Claude Code)
nodes.description: The owner's agentic-jobs analysis (docs/jobs/ - 6 files, 64.6 KB, brought onto this branch from origin/main run 242; 100+ high-signal postings Aug 1 - Sep 6 2026 across 20+ job boards, ~1,365 aggregate roles on frontierroles.com). A LABOR-MARKET signal for where the frontier labs and enterprises are actually investing - a proxy for research direction (the RSI survey / ASPIRE thread: research-direction-setting is the bottleneck). Five organisational patterns, each mapping onto the project's design: (1) DEDICATED HARNESS TEAMS separate from model training (OpenAI Codex Core Agents, Anthropic Claude Managed Agents $405-485K, NVIDIA, DeepSeek, FICO) - harness engineering is infrastructure, not application logic; (2) FORWARD-DEPLOYED ENGINEERING - client-side harness deployment + production instrumentation; (3) EVALUATION AS CI GATE - eval harnesses wired into CI, regressions block releases, near-universal across roles (= the project's exec_guard hook + verify_loop_edit + the acceptor cluster); (4) SELF-IMPROVING AS DEFAULT - reflection/critique/self-debug/meta-agent in 40%+ of roles, Bosch / DeepMind / NVIDIA / startups (= approach_self_improving_harness); (5) TIERED ORCHESTRATION converging as a standard - Tier 1 routers / Tier 2 specialists / Tier 3 utilities, LangGraph state machines, human-in-the-loop handoffs (= the run-218 multi-agent criterion). DeepSeek: 'Model + Harness = Agent'; everything except the core model (tooling, memory, agent loop, desktop, MCP, feedback) is the Harness; a dedicated Agent Harness R&D Engineer + Agent Harness PM whose job includes 'deep collaboration with model training teams to CO-EVOLVE models and harness' - the WHALE / HELIX / JIT-Agent co-evolution thread as a HIRING PRIORITY, benchmarked directly against Claude Code. Anthropic vs OpenAI: Anthropic human-piloted / protocol-first (MCP) / platform-as-infrastructure / outcome-driven execution (specify success criteria + budget, Claude iterates); OpenAI auto-piloted / continuous-learning / vertical. Bearing on the project: strong external validation that Agent = Model + Harness, harness-as-versioned-discipline, verifier-gated self-improvement, and eval-rigs-in-CI are now the INDUSTRY consensus, not a research bet - the project's thesis is where the labor market already is. Recency: Sep 2026, a hiring snapshot (not a result), so it validates direction, not any mechanism.

nodes.label: Don't let the model hold task state in its context: a deterministic task ledger the orchestrator reads/writes; next_ready() is a deterministic pick, sweep_stale() returns claimed-but-abandoned tasks to pending
nodes.description: Built run 244 (tools/task_ledger.py + docs/task_ledger.md), answering the owner's 'tasks get dropped' pain in CLI agent orchestration. Two folded findings say do not let the model hold task state in its context: concept_component_lifecycle_reasoning_degrades_with_size (CordisBench - LLM state-reasoning degrades with system size, a finite reference semantics matches execution exactly) and concept_aspire_... (continued open-ended search erases earlier gains). So: the orchestrator reads and writes a file ledger; the LLM proposes tasks and reports outcomes; the file decides what is ready and what has been dropped. One row per task, statuses pending->active->done (+ blocked / failed / abandoned). Three anti-dropped-task mechanisms: (1) next_ready() is DETERMINISTIC - the oldest pending task whose deps are all done - so the orchestrator reads its next action rather than reasoning about it; (2) sweep_stale(max_active_secs) returns any task claimed but not finished within a timeout back to pending (a worker died / lost context / hit budget), the PILOT supervisor re-dispatch pattern; (3) atomic write via os.replace + an append-only .audit log per mutation. Reference implementation, pure stdlib, NOT wired into the loop - it is the pattern for the owner's orchestrations (poly-bot etc.): copy the one file, replace 'ask the LLM what to do next' with next_ready(), call sweep_stale() each tick, keep the ledger in a durable path. 12 selftest checks.

nodes.label: LLM steering organises into four control surfaces - input (prompt), structural (weights/architecture), state (activations/attentions), output (decoding) - composable via a common pipeline interface; a toolkit lowers the barrier to comparing steering methods
nodes.description: AI Steerability 360 (arXiv:2603.07837, VERIFIED via arXiv abstract read run 245; Mar 2026, IBM; Apache 2.0, HF-native, github.com/IBM/AISteer360). SOURCE: surfaced in the owner's Perplexity deep-research 'Improving Agent Creativity Diversity' (knowledge/notes/2026-09-04-creativity-diversity-mitigation.md on origin/main), section 5 'Quality Variation Mitigation (Better Steering Interfaces)' - cross-checked and folded here. An extensible Python library for steering LLMs, organised around FOUR MODEL CONTROL SURFACES: (1) INPUT - modification of the prompt; (2) STRUCTURAL - modification of weights or architecture; (3) STATE - modification of activations and attentions; (4) OUTPUT - modification of decoding / generation. Steering methods exert control through a common 'steering pipeline' interface that also composes multiple methods; use-case classes define tasks and a benchmark class compares performance. Bearing on the project: the four-surface taxonomy is a clean map of WHERE the model-harness coupling is exercised, and it partitions the project's positions cleanly - INPUT is context/loop_policy + ACE context evolution; STRUCTURAL is the weight-training fork the project declines (WHALE / JIT-Agent); STATE is pattern_activation_probe_monitoring and the context-privesc concern; OUTPUT is the diversity toolkit (verbalized sampling, entropy-max). It also directly addresses concept_human_effort_shifts_from_ideating_to_verifying_and_ownership_is_negotiated's finding that steering SKILL drives output-quality variance - a composable, comparable toolkit lowers the barrier. Currency: Mar 2026 (~6 months old) - a framework/toolkit not a capability claim, so it ages slowly; modest confidence for lack of independent adoption evidence.
