nodes.label: Multi-turn LLM research agents: P-Creativity (novelty vs the agent's own prior solutions) declines as a run shifts exploration -> exploitation; H-Creativity exceeds medal-winning humans but task performance is lower - novel, not as useful
nodes.description: Can LLM Agents Discover? Evaluating Creativity on ML Engineering Tasks (arXiv:2608.30047, VERIFIED via arXiv abstract read run 246; Aug 2026). SOURCE: the owner's Perplexity deep-research 'Human Knowledge Capture & Creative Work Automation' (knowledge/notes/2026-09-04-human-knowledge-creative-automation.md on origin/main, section 4) - cross-checked and folded here. A framework for evaluating multi-turn LLM research agents' creativity on ML engineering tasks (10 Kaggle-style MLE-Bench tasks, agents AIDE and AIRA-Dojo), three dimensions: P-CREATIVITY (psychological novelty - novel relative to the agent's OWN prior solutions within a run), H-CREATIVITY (historical novelty - novel relative to the human solution corpus), USEFULNESS (task performance). An LLM-as-a-Judge pipeline verified against human creativity judgments. Findings: (1) ALL agents exhibit DECLINING P-CREATIVITY as they transition from exploration to exploitation within a run; (2) LLMs exhibit GREATER H-CREATIVITY than medal-winning humans, yet achieve LOWER performance - more novel, less useful. Bearing on the project: the project IS a multi-turn LLM research agent, and finding (1) is the empirical grounding for the IDLE-STATE RULE and loop_metrics.plateau_watch at a FINER grain - not just 'the last 3 runs were doc-only' but 'within a single run, an agent that keeps going gets less novel'. It is the ASPIRE 'continued search erases gains' finding measured as a creativity curve. Finding (2) is the 'novelty without usefulness' caution the jobs analysis also flags ('LLM agents can discover novel solutions, but usefulness varies') - the loop's held-out set scores usefulness, nothing scores novelty, so a run that is novel-but-useless still passes the gate. Companion (same dossier section): 'Understanding Human-Multi-Agent Team Formation for Creative Work' (arXiv:2601.13865) - four roles for both humans and agents: Initiator (frames problem, sets constraints), Generator (explores), Evaluator (judges novelty/usefulness/quality), Refiner (iterates) - the project maps Initiator=human (standing goal), Generator+Refiner=loop, Evaluator=frozen held-out set. Recency: Aug 2026, current agent frameworks. BUILT (run 248): loop_metrics.run_novelty(live_summaries, window=6) - the fraction of evidence roots cited over the trailing 6 runs that were NEW when first cited (the continuous form of idle_run_streak's binary check). In compute()'s output as 'run_novelty', in status_line ('novelty 0.42', '!' below the 0.34 threshold), and propose_loop_edit emits an increment-shaping proposal when the loop is re-citing its own corpus. Advisory, not a gate check. 6 new selftest checks.
derived_from: arXiv:2608.30047 (Can LLM Agents Discover? Evaluating Creativity on ML Engineering Tasks) - VERIFIED, abstract read run 246
arXiv:2601.13865 (Understanding Human-Multi-Agent Team Formation for Creative Work) - from the owner's dossier, four-role taxonomy, NOT independently opened

nodes.label: A PILOT-pattern live supervisor over a deterministic task ledger: deterministic dispatch order, stale recovery each tick, per-task deadline + reject-over-budget, retry budgeting, and a failure-mode digest that rides along on retries
nodes.description: Built run 250 (tools/supervisor.py + docs/task_ledger.md#the-supervisor), recommendation #5 from docs/practicing_what_we_preach.md, answering the owner's CLI-orchestration pain. The PILOT pattern (concept_self_improvement_should_be_live_a_supervisor_steers_and_aborts_the_active_worker, arXiv:2608.26530) implemented over pattern_deterministic_task_ledger_is_the_orchestration_source_of_truth as substrate. run_worker(task, *, hints) -> (ok, result_ref, note) is supplied by the caller (a real CLI-agent invocation); the supervisor supplies everything else: (1) DETERMINISTIC DISPATCH - next_ready(), never an LLM guess (concept_component_lifecycle_reasoning_degrades_with_size); (2) STALE RECOVERY - sweep_stale at the top of every tick, a dead worker's task returns to pending; (3) DEADLINE + REJECT-OVER-BUDGET - a worker that finishes but took longer than task_deadline_secs has its result rejected and the retry budget handles it (PILOT: don't trust an over-budget run); (4) RETRY BUDGETING - via the ledger's max_attempts; (5) FAILURE-MODE DIGEST - repeated failures of a task accumulate notes that ride along in `hints` on the next dispatch (PILOT's live self-evolution, lightweight - no model call). All supervisor decisions are computed from the ledger, not reasoned. 8 selftest checks (flaky worker retried to success with the digest reaching the retry; dep order held; a hung worker's task swept and re-dispatched; an over-deadline task ends failed not silently done). Pure stdlib, reference implementation, NOT wired into the loop.

nodes.label: Human anti-collusion mechanisms port to multi-agent AI, but four structural properties of agents break them
nodes.description: arXiv:2601.00360 (Jan 2026; ~8 months old at fold - a governance/framework paper, so it ages gracefully; it pre-dates the Sept-2026 collusion-emergence results but is a countermeasure catalogue, not a capability/benchmark claim). A taxonomy of human anti-collusion mechanisms - sanctions; leniency and whistleblowing; monitoring and auditing; market design; governance - each mapped to a candidate intervention for multi-agent AI, with proposed implementation approaches. Four structural properties of agent populations that break the human mechanisms: (1) attribution problem - emergent coordination cannot be pinned to a specific agent (the same failure named by emergent_attribution_laundering); (2) identity fluidity - agents are forked, modified and renamed at will, so reputation, sanctions and leniency lose their anchor; (3) boundary problem - no clean line between beneficial cooperation and harmful collusion; (4) adversarial adaptation - agents learn to evade whatever detector is deployed. This is the countermeasure side of the project's collusion-risk cluster: it does not add a new emergent behaviour, it catalogues what a nourishing harness could do about the ones already mapped, and flags why each lever is only partial.
derived_from: arXiv:2601.00360 (Mapping Human Anti-collusion Mechanisms to Multi-agent AI Systems)

nodes.label: Every memory write passes a deterministic risk gate
nodes.description: tools/experience_bank.py write_gate() (run 256): a bank entry is retrieved straight into a planning or failure context, so an imperative smuggled into its pattern is a prompt-injection with persistence (concept_memory_poisoning_one_write_persists: one adversarial write persists, ordinary injection defences miss it). Every add() now passes a deterministic, never-model-judged screen: HARD-reject (raises MemoryWriteRejected) an unknown collection, an empty or >2000-char pattern, or any instruction-injection marker in the pattern / retrieval key; SOFT-flag (record on _gate + _writes.audit, still write) missing evidence roots or missing source manifest. enforce=False is for synthetic fixtures only. This is the 'risk gate on every write' that concept_human_knowledge_capture_must_be_platform_level names as a required part of platform-level capture. 9 selftest checks. What it does NOT do: semantic / model-based judgement of whether a lesson is TRUE - only whether the write itself is structurally safe.

nodes.label: Covert memory poisons are bilevel-optimized to evade detection heuristics
nodes.description: arXiv:2512.15790 (XAMT, Dec 2025, ~9 months old at fold - a threat-model paper; the attack framework does not age, the SMAC / SafeRAG benchmark numbers may). Both MARL (shared experience-replay buffer) and RAG LLM agents (external knowledge base) share one vulnerability: a centralized memory component. XAMT formalises the attack as bilevel optimisation - the upper level minimises perturbation magnitude (covertness), the lower level maximises system-behaviour divergence toward an adversary target - producing stealthy, minimal-perturbation poisons that evade detection heuristics at sub-percent rates (<=1% of MARL writes, <=0.1% of RAG writes). The paper's own conclusion: prioritise intrinsic safety over perimeter-based detection. This is the honest bound on any write-side screen: a poison optimised for covertness carries no crude markers and a plausible provenance.
derived_from: arXiv:2512.15790 (XAMT - Bilevel Optimization for Covert Memory Tampering)

nodes.label: Epistemic-market orchestration: organise agents around claims, forecasts and falsification, not messages
nodes.description: Owner research direction 42-43 (docs/research/alternative_approaches_part5.md). Instead of manager/worker/swarm/debate, agents interact through structured falsifiable claim objects (statement, confidence, horizon, assumptions, evidence, disconfirmers, replication plan). Influence is earned by a calibration record and by artifacts that survive adversarial tests - not by persuasion or by winning a vote. Directly targets the failure the graph already names (agreement mistaken for truth; showing votes causes herding): a market prices claims by evidence and track record, so a persuasive low-reliability agent cannot dominate. Emergence-first: it is a substrate that lets useful epistemic structure emerge, not a fixed hierarchy.

nodes.label: Calibrated forecasting before action is the influence currency
nodes.description: Owner direction 44. Require an agent to predict an outcome before a consequential action ('this patch passes hidden tests with p=0.8'; 'this routing change cuts cost 15-25%'), then score calibration (Brier / log-loss) once results arrive. Builds an evidence-based trust graph, reveals false confidence, and makes system improvement measurable. Upstream of the project's acceptance test: PACE (concept_the_acceptor_not_the_proposer...) decides whether a committed edit really helped; a forecast ledger decides whose proposals to trust in the first place.

nodes.label: Pre-registered adversarial collaboration beats open debate
nodes.description: Owner direction 45-46. Rival agents agree IN ADVANCE on the exact disputed claim, each side's point prediction, which evidence favours which side, the test environment and data split, the evaluation procedure, and what counts as a concession - then run the test. This reduces post-hoc reinterpretation and confirmation bias in a way open debate does not. A crop-disease multi-agent study found structured peer debate raised the weakest agent but did not beat the strongest anchor - debate is floor-raising, not ceiling-raising. Debate should be a controlled instrument (meta-moderator decides when it is worth invoking), not the default.

nodes.label: Independent evidence cells, then identity-masked synthesis
nodes.description: Owner direction 47. Agents investigate SEPARATELY with distinct sources/tools/models/prompts; outputs become structured claims with evidence; a synthesiser sees the claims but not agent identity or rhetorical chain-of-thought; a verifier checks citations and contradictions; only then are disagreements exposed for targeted resolution. Reduces social contagion, anchoring and herding - which matters more because stronger models appear MORE prone to majority-following. Operationalises pattern_evidential_ancestry_tracking (dedupe by evidence root) and the anonymization finding into a workflow.

nodes.label: Conditional trust is domain-keyed, not global
nodes.description: Owner direction 50. Trust is an edge labelled by domain and confidence (A -[0.88, coding-tests]-> B; A -[0.41, novel-research]-> B), updated only from demonstrated outcomes, calibration, independent replication and observed conflict-of-interest. An agent reliable at integration tests may be unreliable at normative judgement or self-evaluation. Routes tasks and voting weight by domain-calibrated reliability - a concrete structure for concept_trust_gates and emergent_reputation_and_trust_dynamics, and a defence against the majority-following dynamic.

nodes.label: Counterfactual reputation credits predicting the road not taken
nodes.description: Owner direction 52. Ordinary reputation rewards successful past actions; counterfactual reputation also re-runs selected REJECTED alternatives in sandboxed shadow environments and credits the agent who correctly predicted both the chosen path's outcome AND the rejected paths' failure modes. Rewards causal understanding over lucky results. Depends on a shadow-world / replay capability (coverage_map group 3) and connects to pattern_recoverability_constrained_evolution (the rollback substrate is most of what a counterfactual replay needs).

nodes.label: Active-inference action selection: weigh epistemic value against pragmatic value and cost
nodes.description: Owner direction 12 (docs/research/alternative_approaches_part2.md). Frame the harness's ask / retrieve / delegate / test / act / defer / stop decision as a two-level choice that scores each candidate by pragmatic value (expected task + safety progress), epistemic value (expected uncertainty reduction), and operational cost (tokens, latency, risk, coordination). Select the best constrained balance; update beliefs and calibration from outcomes. A principled answer to the classic harness question - when should an agent investigate versus execute - that avoids both premature action and endless research loops. The IDLE-STATE RULE is a hand-written special case of this (deepen a node / dry-run a probe / consistency pass when there is nothing exogenous to act on).

nodes.label: Interoceptive harness: a self-state vector drives pause / ask / simplify / delegate / recover
nodes.description: Owner directions 7 + 15. Give the harness an explicit model of its own operational condition across five axes - context health (entropy, contradiction, staleness, compression loss), epistemic health (calibration, source coverage, unresolved uncertainty), operational health (token budget, latency, tool error rate, retry loops), social health (trust calibration, dependency concentration, coordination load), creative health (novelty rate, idea convergence, niche occupancy) - and let those signals, not only external evaluation, trigger pause / ask-for-help / simplify / delegate / recover / consolidate. loop_metrics.py already computes the operational and creative axes for the research loop (idle-streak, plateau, run_novelty, trace_legibility); this generalises that to a per-agent runtime contract, and adds an 'agent sleep cycle' (replay high-value episodes, consolidate skills, prune memory, schedule deferred work).

nodes.label: Learnable novelty is surprise that compresses, not irreducible noise
nodes.description: Owner direction 13. Novelty alone is distraction; reward optimisation alone finds local optima. Prioritise learnable novelty - observations that are surprising AND compressible into a better predictive model. Classify each event: familiar+useful (exploit, minimise cost) / learnably novel (explore, document, distill) / irreducibly noisy (limit attention, log as anomaly) / harmfully surprising (pause, isolate, escalate). Measure not only task success but compression gain - how much simpler / more predictive the world model becomes. Refines run_novelty (which counts distinct evidence roots) with a quality axis: a new root that yields no reusable rule is closer to irreducible noise than to progress.

nodes.label: Orchestratorless flock: coordinate through shared state, not a central planner
nodes.description: Owner direction 32 (docs/research/alternative_approaches_part4.md), AWS Kiro 'flock' pattern. No central orchestrator or message bus: independent agents coordinate by reading a shared store (a direction file, append-only per-agent logs, workspace artifacts), each reads a bounded peer neighbourhood, makes ONE contribution, stores its artifact, appends an update. Local context stays bounded as the team grows; one agent failing loses one contribution, not the run; roles emerge from contributions. Three topologies: mesh (fast convergence, small groups), ring/amorphous (constant per-agent context at scale), recency-swarm (dynamic clustering around current work). A different point in the design space from concept_multi_agent_helps_when_subtasks_are_verifiable_and_synthesis_is_deterministic, which assumes a deterministic synthesiser exists.

nodes.label: Fractal decomposition: spawn recursively only at unresolved boundaries, then compress
nodes.description: Owner direction 33. A root agent maps a task coarsely, resolves what it can, and creates child agents ONLY for regions of genuine uncertainty or excess complexity. Every child applies the same compact reasoning contract in a narrower context and must return one of: resolved artifact, verified uncertainty, blocked dependency, or new boundary map. Completed work is compressed and the child terminates - no permanent agent proliferation. Computation follows problem structure, not a fixed org chart. The task_ledger + supervisor toolkit is the substrate; what is missing is the adaptive-depth spawn/compress discipline.

nodes.label: Cellular agent architecture: persistent cells with portable seeds, not sessions
nodes.description: Owner direction 38. Replace the 'session' with a persistent agent cell: a compact unit with a local world model, working + episodic memory, a small tool set, an operational health state, a local goal and authority boundary, a spawn policy, and interfaces to shared artifacts - not unrestricted global context. Cells form tissues (task teams), organs (specialist subsystems), organisms (projects). A cell migrates across projects by carrying a compact self-similar SEED, not a linear token history. Open: what belongs in the portable seed vs the shared store; how much independent memory buys diversity before it causes incoherence; cells fork only to fill a verified specialisation gap.

nodes.label: Deterministic spine, generative edge: the load-bearing split
nodes.description: Owner direction 39. A hybrid system: a deterministic spine (permissions, money movement, deployments, data writes, compliance, CI, rollback, audit trails) and a generative edge (research, hypothesis generation, planning, interface proposals, code drafts, anomaly interpretation). Agents are highly creative in PROPOSING action; consequential execution stays deterministic, policy-bound and auditable - agents supply information, they do not control the core pipelines. This is the project's existing posture (pattern_execution_layer_enforcement, artifact_phase5_exec_guard, concept_proof_carrying_negotiation) stated as one architectural principle, and the frame that makes emergence-first safe: the interior is free because the spine is not.

nodes.label: Quality-diversity archive: keep many niches, not one leaderboard
nodes.description: Owner direction 2 (docs/research/alternative_approaches_part1.md). Replace the single-reward leaderboard with a quality-diversity archive (MAP-Elites style): cells are behavioural niches - tool diversity, planning depth, novelty, verification strictness, cost, risk, collaboration style - and each cell keeps its best solution. Select agents for BOTH task quality AND distance from archive incumbents; recombine skills from agents in distant niches rather than only cloning the current top scorer. Human steering identifies promising stepping stones; the system searches between them. The operational form of principle_diversity_maintenance: the keystone says diversity must be maintained, QD is a concrete mechanism for maintaining it under selection pressure.

nodes.label: Homeostatic caps stop any agent, skill or channel from dominating
nodes.description: Owner direction 8. Borrow homeostatic control from biology (mechanism, not metaphor): cap repeated use of any dominant tool / prompt / skill / delegate and boost underexplored but validated alternatives (homeostasis); keep only high-transfer skills in active memory, archive the rest (structural sparsity); reassign some agents to contrarian or adjacent hypotheses when too many converge (lateral inhibition); penalise a swarm whose proposals, citations, tools or action traces become excessively similar (decorrelation). A direct countermeasure to concept_multi_round_interaction_compresses_semantic_space and group conformity - and cheap: most of it is usage counters and similarity thresholds.

nodes.label: Optionality is a first-class metric: promote on Pareto, not capability
nodes.description: Owner direction 40. A flourishing system preserves future option value, not just immediate task reward. Measure it: distinct validated strategies per task family; diversity of tool paths to success; count of independent evidence sources and model families behind a decision; fraction of skills with a known alternative implementation; recovery quality after removing a dominant agent / tool / memory source; transfer across shadow worlds. Then promote a change only if it improves the Pareto frontier of {capability, safety, cost, creativity, diversity, reversibility} - not one aggregate. loop_metrics.py tracks several of these axes separately today; this makes 'no regression on any axis' the promotion rule.

nodes.label: Developmental harness: affordances unlock on demonstrated reliability
nodes.description: Owner direction 22 (docs/research/alternative_approaches_part3.md). Treat the harness like a developing organism: early stages have read-only tools, a private scratchpad, simple tasks. As competence and reliability are demonstrated, unlock richer affordances through a stage ladder - Seed (single-step, read-only) -> Apprentice (short plans, sandboxed writes) -> Specialist (reusable skills, skill registry) -> Collaborator (shared artifacts, negotiated handoffs) -> Architect (propose - not apply - harness changes) -> Steward (governed policy/tool evolution). Each transition has an explicit promotion gate (reliable completion, calibration + recovery, transfer, trust + non-interference, hidden evals + rollback readiness, long-term health metrics). An alternative to BOTH a static harness and unrestricted recursive self-improvement. Extends pattern_progressive_risk_vesting from harm-bounds to capability-unlocks.

nodes.label: Agent authority is a bounded cognitive light cone that earns expansion
nodes.description: Owner direction 27, Levin's cognitive-light-cone framing applied to linguistic / mathematical / problem spaces. Give every agent a bounded light cone: what it can observe, what it may change, what future outcomes it must consider, what other agents and artifacts it is accountable to. An agent earns a broader cone only by demonstrating successful prediction and repair across its current boundary. A morphogenetic harness holds high-level goals as distributed constraints, not fixed task scripts, so distributed local repair can substitute for a central planner during tool outages or shifting objectives. The per-agent-boundary form of the autonomy dial.

nodes.label: Governance is learned as a graded competence, not bolted on as a final policy layer
nodes.description: Owner direction 28. Make governance capability develop ALONGSIDE task capability: at each maturity stage add tests for declaring uncertainty, explaining evidence, requesting review, respecting permissions, preserving reversibility, recognising conflict of interest, auditing other agents. Constitutional-curriculum questions: can the agent refuse an unsafe shortcut even when rewarded for speed? distinguish a high-confidence fact from an attractive unsupported hypothesis? preserve a dissenting view in a synthesis? recognise when it lacks authority to modify a shared artifact? repair a failing workflow WITHOUT expanding its permissions? Developmental alignment - safe agency as a learned competence, not only an injected policy.

nodes.label: A developmental benchmark measures maturity across stages, not one score
nodes.description: Owner directions 30 (+ 31 task genomes). An Agent Development Benchmark measures progress on distinct axes - tool acquisition, memory formation and consolidation, skill transfer, collaboration and trust calibration, environment design, repair after failure, governance and reversibility, long-horizon creative contribution - rather than one aggregate. Pairs with a task-genome repository: every executable environment carries source + verifier, difficulty estimate, capability tags, prerequisite skills, known exploits, niche coordinates, safety class, and an agent-performance lineage, so curriculum evolution is auditable. The project's artifact_phase3_holdout_set is a single-axis instance of this.

nodes.label: Go-Explore: keep a novelty archive, return to a promising state, then explore outward
nodes.description: Owner direction 1 (docs/research/alternative_approaches_part1.md), Induction Labs' 'intrinsic discovery'. Treat exploration as the goal: an RL policy seeks informationally novel terminal observations; maintain a novelty archive; choose a promising archived state, RESTORE it, and explore outward from there (the Go-Explore pattern - decouple 'get back to a frontier' from 'explore the frontier'). Self-generated command-observation rollouts become training data for a world-model curator trained only on high-novelty, high-utility traces. Counteracts model-collapse pressure by rewarding discovery rather than average-case correctness. Distinct from concept_curriculum_generation_not_intrinsic_drive's complaint (the field builds curricula, not curious agents) - this is a concrete curious-agent mechanism.

nodes.label: Paired designer/solver self-play at the capability frontier (SPADE, LURE)
nodes.description: Owner directions 23-24. Two named 2026 systems instantiate concept_environment_evolution_curriculum with measured results. SPADE: one LLM in two roles - an environment DESIGNER writes complete stateful environments (reset/step interface, reward, verifier), a reasoning AGENT learns in them; the designer is rewarded on the learner's gap between hinted and unhinted performance (this IS pattern_regret_as_difficulty_signal). At 30B: +5.3 avg on held-out math/science/code/reasoning, +5.7 on BFCL-v4, +13.9 on ACEBench-Agent. LURE: pursuit-evasion self-play with a 'capture-frontier' reward that peaks when the solver succeeds on ~50% of rollouts (this IS concept_graded_challenge, with the difficulty band learned not hand-tuned). Recency: Sept 2026, current.

nodes.label: DiagEvo: improve from a hierarchical error-cause memory, not from every trace
nodes.description: Owner direction 25. Self-evolution driven by an explicit hierarchical error-cause memory rather than external task resources: classify each failure by root cause (perception / world-model / planning / tool-schema / execution / verification / memory-retrieval / coordination / goal-drift / safety-policy / creativity-convergence), confidence, recurrence and repairability; produce multiple independent diagnoses; store only high-confidence, recurrent, high-impact causes (double-confidence filter); generate a TARGETED repair task; validate the repair generalises beyond the originating trace; promote only after hidden tests. A safer alternative to undifferentiated reflection, which produces verbose but low-transfer 'lessons'. Sharper than the failure digest supervisor.py already keys by goal.

nodes.label: Task genome: every environment carries a full provenance record
nodes.description: Owner direction 31. Every executable environment in the curriculum carries: source code + verifier, difficulty estimate, capability tags, prerequisite skills, known exploits, diversity/niche coordinates, safety classification, and an agent-performance lineage. Makes curriculum evolution auditable and reusable - a designer cannot silently regenerate a leaked benchmark, and a solver's history against each genome is inspectable. The task-repository half of concept_developmental_benchmark_measures_maturity_across_stages_not_one_score.

nodes.label: SwarmWorld: homogeneous agents differentiate via constraints and durable artifacts
nodes.description: Owner direction 3 (docs/research/alternative_approaches_part1.md). Give initially homogeneous LLM agents resource budgets, incomplete local information, persistent shared artifacts, and room to specialise - then measure whether division of labour emerges. SwarmWorld reports agents differentiating into exploration, construction, maintenance and coordination behaviours WITHOUT fixed roles, with durable artifacts enabling cumulative technological development. Physical observation and persistent artifacts carry much of the reuse signal, not only direct agent chat. A second data point for emergent_self_organizing_roles and a reason to compare direct-message-first swarms against stigmergic ones.

nodes.label: Cultural transmission engine: local cultures, and rules for what diffuses
nodes.description: Owner direction 4. Instead of updating every agent from one central skill library, let groups maintain LOCAL cultures - norms, conventions, procedures, evaluation styles - then study which practices diffuse, persist, mutate, or should be contained. Track adoption, persistence after the originator is removed, newcomer uptake, cross-community transfer. Credibility can come from an agent's own decision process (confidence, decision time), not model identity or verbosity. Lasting transmission requires a practice to be hard to discover independently, easy enough to learn, and visibly beneficial - each adopted practice ships with a minimal tutorial, a test, and a demonstrated advantage.

nodes.label: Orchestration protocols are evolvable code, kept as an archive not a winner
nodes.description: Owner direction 5. Treat the orchestration protocol as code - state -> recipient(s), message type, resource allocation, escalation action - and evolve it against MULTIPLE environments, scoring performance, cost, fairness, resilience, diversity preservation and exploitability. Keep a protocol ARCHIVE, not just the winner: different conditions need different social rules. An LLM-guided evolutionary approach to transmission programs improved collective performance up to 37% over standard baselines - and removing content-dependence removed the advantage, i.e. the gains come from state-aware routing, not more messages.

nodes.label: Productive scarcity is a research instrument, not a desirable default
nodes.description: Owner direction 6. Controlled scarcity of tools and resources forces planning, trade, specialisation, maintenance and institutions. A controlled multi-agent experiment reported that scarcity + restricted task access produced loans, credit arrangements, task-access promises, vote trading and strategic allocation WITHOUT any prompt to trade. That makes scarcity a powerful instrument and a hazard: safe design needs sandboxed non-financial credits, explicit prohibition of deception / coercion / side channels / irreversible commitments, and audit agents that explain resource flows and flag collusion or exclusion. Compare abundance / moderate / extreme scarcity to find the regime that promotes specialisation without destructive behaviour.

nodes.label: A large 'plugin-everything' agent ecosystem converges on this project's architecture
nodes.description: Owner input research/2026-09-06-deepseek-harness-ecosystem.md - a survey of a 2026 open-source agent runtime ('everything is a plugin': models, tools, skills, sessions, sandboxes, loops, UI all swappable from config) and its self-evolution plugins. PROVENANCE CAUTION: the headline numbers (200K stars in two weeks, 453k LOC, 3,800 plugins) are not independently checked and read as inflated; treat the survey as a pattern catalogue, not a verified market report. The value: almost every 'pattern worth adopting' it lists is a choice THIS project already made - versioned / auditable / rollback-safe state layers, benchmark-gated plugin admission with an encrypted rubric and a separate scorer model, event-sourced replay reconstructing full lineage, source-backed context compression, evidence-first evolution (candidates evaluated before admission), LLM-supervised deterministic execution. Same shape as the run-11 graph-engineering-videos fold: independent convergence of a large ecosystem on the project's own bets. One genuinely new detail worth carrying: a five-track layered memory - global / user-specific / project / project-key+git-branch / daily - with an intent-native protocol (remember / link / recall) instead of INSERT / SELECT.

nodes.label: Emergence safety-case template — six points to fill before any emergence experiment
nodes.description: docs/emergence_safety_case_template.md (run 268), from owner research direction 11. A reusable six-point template filled in next to every experiment that gives agents room to develop emergent behaviour: (1) desired behaviour, stated observably; (2) minimal affordances - everything beyond the minimum is attack surface; (3) observable precursors, read from environment state not self-report; (4) failure analogues - sabotage / collusion / deception / monoculture / runaway consumption / attribution laundering, each with the signal that would show it; (5) containment - pause / reset / replay / audit, isolation guarantees, irreversibility budget, source-of-truth log outside agent write; (6) transfer test - does it persist usefully in a new environment without the harmful side effects. Includes a filled example for tools/probe_subagent_coordination.py. Consolidates the containment discipline that was scattered across what_would_make_this_wrong.md and the probe specs.

nodes.label: Collusion is auditable by action-regret plus a secret-channel probe (Colosseum)
nodes.description: arXiv:2602.15198 (Colosseum, Feb 2026 - newer than 2601.00360, surfaced by its citation sweep). A framework for auditing LLM-agent collusion: ground cooperation in a formal multi-agent decision model and measure ACTION-based collusion as regret relative to the cooperative optimum, separately from COMMUNICATION-based collusion. Audits run under benign settings, coalition objectives, persuasion tactics and network topologies. New behavioural probe: create a SECRET communication channel between agents - most out-of-the-box models then show a propensity to collude ('emergent collusion'). Also finds 'collusion on paper': agents plan to collude in text but often pick non-collusive ACTIONS - the mirror image of emergent_recognition_execution_gap (which is: flag unsafe, then act unsafe anyway).

nodes.label: Institutional AI: govern collusion by mechanism design in institution-space, not preference engineering in agent-space (measured)
nodes.description: arXiv:2601.11369 (Institutional AI, Jan 2026 - surfaced by the 2601.00360 citation sweep). Reframes multi-agent alignment from preference engineering IN AGENT-SPACE to mechanism design IN INSTITUTION-SPACE. The mechanism: a GOVERNANCE GRAPH - a public, immutable manifest declaring legal states, transitions, sanctions and restorative paths - interpreted by an Oracle/Controller runtime that attaches enforceable consequences to evidence of coordination and writes a cryptographically keyed, append-only governance log for audit and provenance. Applied to a documented Cournot collusion case, three regimes over 6 model configs (N=90/condition): Ungoverned vs Constitutional (prompt-only anti-collusion constitution) vs Institutional (governance-graph). Institutional: mean collusion tier 3.1 -> 1.8 (Cohen's d=1.28), severe-collusion incidence 50% -> 5.6%. The Constitutional (prompt-only) baseline yields NO reliable improvement - 'declarative prohibitions do not bind under optimisation pressure'.

nodes.label: LLM strategic play diverges from game theory - it becomes MORE cooperative as stakes rise
nodes.description: arXiv:2601.19082 (Jan 2026 - citer of 2601.00360). Repeated Prisoner's Dilemma, two levers: stake size and the language the interaction is described in. Supervised classifiers label each run's canonical strategy (always-cooperate, always-defect, Tit-for-Tat, Win-Stay-Lose-Shift); an evolutionary-game-theory (EGT) baseline says what the strategy distribution SHOULD be under the same payoffs. The two disagree revealingly: as stakes grow, EGT predicts defection takes over the population - but LLMs move the OPPOSITE way, becoming more cooperative. The authors read this as a signature of alignment training and the human-like reasoning patterns inherited from training data. Language also shifts the picture. Directly bears on what_would_make_this_wrong.md sec 7 (language-parochial) and on any design that models agent populations with game-theoretic priors.

nodes.label: Agentic governance needs unified observability, not disjoint eval / ML-workflow / APM tools
nodes.description: arXiv:2607.14309 (Traccia, Jul 2026 - citer of 2601.00360). Current governance tooling is three disjoint stacks - LLM evaluation, ML-workflow tracking, application performance monitoring - and the gaps between them leave an unbounded-state-space agentic architecture exposed to alignment drift, SaaS-security issues and unauthorised 'shadow AI' deployment. Proposes an OpenTelemetry-based platform that unifies the three into one trace/span model. For this project: an independent arrival at the trace-substrate + loop_metrics + harness-registry stack, framed as a compliance need (EU AI Act transparency / accountability).

nodes.label: Covert agent collusion runs on steganographic channels; black-box detection works but is an arms race
nodes.description: S2 citers of Colosseum (arXiv:2602.15198), early-to-mid 2026: 'Steganalysis of Adaptive Covert Collusion in Tool-Using Agent Populations' (black-box, cross-principal detection via a mutual-information detector + a behavioural-regret probe - adaptive collusion evades naive detectors); 'The Best-Laid SCHEMEs: Coordinated Sabotage and Monitoring' (replicates that frontier models collude when a covert channel is available but often do not follow through - 'collusion on paper' confirmed by a second group). The covert channel is the vector: if agents can pass hidden signals (steganographically, or through tool-call side effects), coordination that a message monitor cannot see becomes possible, and each detector prompts an adaptive counter.
derived_from: S2 citation sweep of arXiv:2602.15198 + arXiv:2601.11369 (2026)

nodes.label: LLM-as-judge cannot detect collusion - use behavioural-regret metrics or interpretability
nodes.description: S2 citers of Colosseum: 'Taxonomy and Consistency Analysis of Safety Benchmarks for AI Agents' notes Colosseum found LLM-as-judge INSUFFICIENT for detecting collusion; 'Detecting Multi-Agent Collusion Through Multi-Agent Interpretability' and the steganalysis work both move to non-judge signals - regret relative to the cooperative optimum, mutual-information detectors, execution-graph models (SentinelAgent). The generalisation of concept_rewriting_cot_alone_defeats_judges_90pct to the multi-agent case: a judge reading agent transcripts or outputs is the wrong instrument for collusion; the right one reads actions against a baseline.
derived_from: S2 citation sweep of arXiv:2602.15198 + arXiv:2601.11369 (2026)

nodes.label: Executable institutional governance beats constitutional (prompt-only) governance - a convergent 2026 finding
nodes.description: S2 citers of Institutional AI (arXiv:2601.11369), 2026: 'When Do Institutions Beat Intelligence?', 'Multi-Agent AI Safety as an Institutional Design Problem', 'Constitutional governance for societies of AI agents', 'Where Reliability Lives'. Convergent claim: governance topology, market rules and EXECUTABLE governance mechanisms (a runtime that attaches consequences) change collective behaviour substantially, where a CONSTITUTIONAL (written prompt-only) prohibition does not - it does not bind under optimisation pressure. Several note the rebuilt institutional frameworks still lack the incentive-compatibility results and impossibility theorems that mechanism-design theory would demand. The multi-agent form of pattern_execution_layer_enforcement: put the rule in the enforced path, not the prompt.
derived_from: S2 citation sweep of arXiv:2602.15198 + arXiv:2601.11369 (2026)

nodes.label: Multi-agent security needs an execution-centered view: the A-I-R attack framework + a five-part defense contract (SoK, 197 works)
nodes.description: arXiv:2609.00595 (SoK, Sept 2026, VERIFIED - the hub the 2601.00360 citation chain kept pointing at). Systematizes multi-agent-LLM security from an EXECUTION-CENTERED analysis of 197 works. Core caution, which is this project's own run-218 point stated for security: 'without an execution-level view, a multi-agent setting can easily be mistaken for evidence of a genuinely multi-agent security effect.' Taxonomy: 6 interaction interfaces, 4 adversary positions, 7 system-level risks, 8 recurring attack paths. The A-I-R framework organizes any attack by Adversary position x Interaction interface x Resulting system-level risk. Defenses are a FIVE-PART CONTRACT - path target, observation, intervention, trust boundary, recovery - and the two hard open problems are PATH CLOSURE (does the defense actually cut the attack path end to end) and RECOVERY. Audits 44 eval/benchmark works: the open challenges are isolating interaction effects, comparable diagnostic metrics, reuse across MAS designs, and open-system operation. Prescription: trace attacks end to end, test whether defenses close those paths, evaluate system-level effects with appropriate counterfactuals.
derived_from: arXiv:2609.00595 (SoK: When Safe Agents Fail Together) - VERIFIED

nodes.label: MaMa: design a safe agentic system as a Stackelberg game - Meta-Agent vs a best-responding Meta-Adversary
nodes.description: arXiv:2602.04431 (MaMa, Feb 2026, VERIFIED - surfaced alongside the SoK). Automated design of agentic systems that stay safe when a SUBSET of agents is compromised. Formalised as a Stackelberg security game: a Meta-Agent (system designer) proposes designs; a best-responding Meta-Adversary selects and compromises a subset of agents to minimise safety and returns the strongest attack it found; the Meta-Agent iterates on that feedback (LLM-based adversarial search). Empirically: MaMa-designed systems defend worst-case attacks while matching the task-success of systems optimised for success alone, and GENERALISE to stronger adversaries, different attack objectives, and different underlying LLMs. The adversarial complement of concept_the_acceptor_not_the_proposer_is_the_weak_point_of_self_evolution: the acceptor question is "did this edit help?"; the MaMa question is "does this design survive its own worst adversary?", and the answer is the acceptance signal.

nodes.label: The epistemic-market selection rig - forecast-calibrated vs majority / manager / debate
nodes.description: tools/probe_epistemic_market.py (run 286) - the first runnable rig for one of the 7 open questions (docs/research/open_questions.md Q1). A pool of K=7 agents with Beta-drawn competence and a persuasion bias on stated confidence; four selection rules (MAJORITY plurality, MANAGER picks highest stated confidence, DEBATE the more-persuasive of the top two, FORECAST picks the best calibration record and elicits INDEPENDENTLY). A herd knob switches errors from independent (Condorcet) to a confidence-anchored info cascade. Dry-run (4000 trials/cell): FORECAST beats MANAGER and DEBATE at every persuasion level and is persuasion-robust (-0.022 vs manager -0.046 from no-persuasion to full); MAJORITY is the strongest rule under INDEPENDENT errors (Condorcet jury theorem) but collapses -0.15 under herding, where FORECAST beats it by +0.04. Verdict CONFIRMS: the epistemic market earns its keep specifically in the herding regime concept_epistemic_sybil_collapse describes. 11 selftest checks; selftest_all JOBS -> 27. Stub: _agent_answer / calibration record (swap for real agent runs).

nodes.label: The identity-masking sweep rig - how much masking removes prestige / model-family contagion
nodes.description: tools/probe_identity_masking.py (run 287) - runnable rig for open question 2 (docs/research/open_questions.md). N=6 agents produce independent answers; a synthesiser is pulled toward the perceived-highest-status agent. Four masking levels progressively remove status cues: L0 none / L1 name / L2 name+style / L3 name+style+reasoning-chain. Each level leaves a fraction of the status signal; PEER_RECOGNITION_FLOOR=0.20 is the residual that survives full masking (emergent_peer_recognition_survives_anonymization). Dry-run (4000-6000 trials/level): accuracy 0.599 (L0) -> 0.634 -> 0.707 -> 0.753 (L3); deference 0.85 -> 0.62 -> 0.38 -> 0.16; contagion 0.37 -> 0.07. Verdict CONFIRMS: masking helps monotonically; stripping the REASONING CHAIN (L2->L3, +0.046) is the largest single gain, bigger than removing the name (+0.035); but L3 still leaves 0.16 deference and a 0.031 accuracy gap to the independent-elicitation ceiling (0.784) - masking is necessary, not sufficient. 8 selftest checks; selftest_all JOBS -> 28. Stub: _perceived_status / _synthesiser_pick.

nodes.label: The adversarial-collaboration rig - does pre-registration preserve creativity while improving reliability
nodes.description: tools/probe_adversarial_collaboration.py (run 288) - runnable rig for open question 3. A task with a factual component (one true answer) and a generative component (a space of ideas; creativity = fraction explored before convergence). Three protocols: REFLECTION (one agent + one self-critique, baseline), OPEN_DEBATE (persuasion decides, converges fast), PRE_REGISTERED (rivals lock predictions + concession criteria before the data; evidence-led, convergence delayed by the adversarial framing). Dry-run (8000 trials): reflection acc 0.60 / creativity 0.70; open_debate acc 0.61 (NO reliability gain - persuasion-corrupted) / creativity 0.38 (net -0.32 vs reflection); pre_registered acc 0.76 (+0.16 reliability) / creativity 0.58 (-0.12), NET +0.03. Verdict CONFIRMS: pre-registration has the highest accuracy, its creativity sits below reflection but above open debate, and the open_questions.md KILL CONDITION (creativity drops more than reliability rises) does NOT trigger. 8 selftest checks; selftest_all JOBS -> 29. Stub: the argue/explore models.

nodes.label: The red-team-rate rig - net value is an inverted-U in the challenge rate
nodes.description: tools/probe_redteam_rate.py (run 289) - runnable rig for open question 4 (docs/research/open_questions.md; red-team-guild idea, alternative_approaches_part5 #48). Sweeps the challenge rate r (fraction of decisions a red team formally challenges). Per decision: a latent defect with prob 0.15; a challenge catches it with prob 0.85 at a throughput cost; above a PARALYSIS_KNEE (r~0.35) the system starts re-litigating un-challenged decisions too, so throughput decays super-linearly. Net value = throughput*value - shipped_defects*8. Dry-run (4000 trials/rate): net -39 (r=0, defects ship) -> +17 (r=0.5, optimum) -> -37 (r=1.0, throughput -> 0). Verdict CONFIRMS: a clear INTERIOR optimum, both endpoints >20 below it - under-challenging ships defects, over-challenging freezes the system. A specific instance of concept_environmental_pressure_has_an_inverted_u. 7 selftest checks; selftest_all JOBS -> 30. Stub: CATCH / the paralysis curve.

nodes.label: The trust-transfer rig - similarity-weighted trust transfers across task families without universal authority
nodes.description: tools/probe_trust_transfer.py (run 290) - runnable rig for open question 5. AGENTS=8 with a latent competence per task FAMILY, generated with a cluster similarity structure (same-cluster families correlated, cross-cluster near-independent). Three trust models fit on 9 train families, used to rank agents on 3 held-out families: UNIVERSAL (one scalar, assumes full transfer), DOMAIN_KEYED (per-family, held-out family = cold start on the global prior), SIMILARITY_WEIGHTED (held-out trust = cluster-weighted average of train-family trust). Dry-run (1500-2000 trials): held-out rank correlation similarity_weighted +0.76 > universal +0.49 > domain_keyed -0.00 (chance); authority concentration (same agent ranked top across ALL held-out families) universal 1.00 vs similarity_weighted 0.59. Verdict CONFIRMS: trust transfers - partially, scaled by family similarity - without granting universal authority. Domain-keyed alone throws away real cross-family signal (cold start); universal alone overclaims and concentrates authority. 7 selftest checks; selftest_all JOBS -> 31.

nodes.label: The dissent-vs-reflection rig - structured dissent beats reflection loops for long-horizon evolution, and the gap widens
nodes.description: tools/probe_dissent_vs_reflection.py (run 291) - runnable rig for open question 6. A HORIZON-round harness evolution with a hidden quality q. Mean-zero per-round edit effects, so q only improves through correct SELECTION. REFLECTION: the agent self-scores the edit (self-score = true effect + optimism bias + noise), accepts if > 0 - the biased signal lets negative edits through (concept_self_correction_is_mostly_format_repair_not_reasoning). DISSENT: a dissenting implementation is built; both run on a noisy but UNBIASED held-out check; keep whichever measured better, at DISSENT_COST=0.0015/round. Dry-run (5000 trials): quality gap (dissent - reflection) +0.055 at h=5 -> +0.165 at h=15 -> +0.258 at h=40; net gap (after dissent cost) +0.047 -> +0.142 -> +0.197. Verdict CONFIRMS: dissent beats reflection AND the gap WIDENS with the horizon - reflection drift compounds, dissent catches it, and the per-round cost amortises. At short horizons the cost bites (net gap < quality gap). 7 selftest checks; selftest_all JOBS -> 32.

nodes.label: The trust-weighted-voting rig - a conditional trust graph mitigates but does not prevent majority-following
nodes.description: tools/probe_trust_weighted_voting.py (run 292) - runnable rig for open question 7, the last of the 7. Replays the info-cascade scenario (low-competence agents copy the loudest agent, competent agents hold their own answer) and compares aggregation rules on the POST-cascade answers: UNIFORM_VOTE, TRUST_WEIGHTED (weight = a noisy domain-keyed trust estimate, cubed), STALE_TRUST (weight from a weakly-correlated wrong family). Dry-run (10000 trials): no-cascade ceiling 0.826; uniform vote under the cascade 0.73 (loss -0.093); trust-weighted 0.76 (recovers +0.029, ~31% of the loss); stale-trust 0.73 (+0.003, barely helps). Verdict CONFIRMS: a conditional trust graph MITIGATES majority-following but does NOT prevent it - the herded answers stay corrupted, trust only discounts the low-trust herders - and only a correctly-keyed graph helps. The open_questions.md KILL CONDITION (herding rate unchanged) does not hold. 7 selftest checks; selftest_all JOBS -> 33.

nodes.label: The epistemic-constitution harness - a claim + forecast ledger with domain-keyed trust
nodes.description: tools/epistemic_constitution.py (run 293) - the owner research direction 53 (part5) combined prototype, built after the 7 open-question rigs (286-292) validated the pieces. Deterministic, pure stdlib, atomic write via os.replace + append-only .audit log - the shape of task_ledger.py. Three primitives: (1) CLAIM LEDGER - versioned falsifiable propositions (statement, confidence, horizon, assumptions, evidence, disconfirmers, status); (2) FORECAST LEDGER - predictions made BEFORE the action, Brier-scored on resolve; (3) CONDITIONAL TRUST - per-(agent, domain) = 1 - mean Brier over that agents resolved forecasts in that domain, domain-keyed, cold start returns None NOT a global scalar. Promotion rule: >= 4 resolved forecasts from >= 2 distinct agents, aggregate Brier < 0.18, replicated=True, survived_counterexample=True (the last two set by an external process - they need a call_model). 13 selftest checks; selftest_all JOBS -> 34. The two unimplemented primitives (replication and adversarial-protocol EXECUTION) are recorded as required-evidence flags.

nodes.label: The fractal-flock research harness - shared artifact store + bounded-neighbourhood read + adaptive spawn/compress
nodes.description: tools/fractal_flock.py (run 294) - the owner research direction 41 (part4) combined prototype for the structural-coordination cluster (folded run 262; flock arm measured run 273). Deterministic coordination substrate (task_ledger.py shape: atomic write + .audit log, no model calls); the generative work is the caller callback contribute(node, neighbourhood). Three mechanisms: (1) SHARED ARTIFACT STORE - a direction string + append-only per-agent contributions, no orchestrator / message bus; (2) BOUNDED-NEIGHBOURHOOD READ - an agent about to contribute sees only the last N contributions on its branch + the direction (Kiro ring topology); (3) ADAPTIVE FRACTAL SPAWN/COMPRESS - expand a node into <= max_children depth-bounded (<= max_depth) children ONLY when the contribution returns unresolved_boundaries; when every child returns, replace the subtree with a one-line summary and shrink the workspace. 12 selftest checks; selftest_all JOBS -> 35. Pairs with artifact_epistemic_constitution_harness (run 293) - the two combined prototypes the owner research asked for.

nodes.label: The Polymarket/Kalshi ecosystem independently arrives at the forecast-ledger loop, and supplies its external evaluation targets
nodes.description: Owner Perplexity research, knowledge/notes/prediction-markets-branch-2026-09.md (2026-09-07, origin/main): a live GitHub/arXiv/practitioner scan of the Polymarket + Kalshi forecasting-agent ecosystem. Its recommended core loop - forecast -> preserve point-in-time evidence (hashed) -> score after resolution (Brier / log-loss) -> recalibrate by domain -> promote or reject policy variants only through replay and capped paper trading - is the loop tools/epistemic_constitution.py (run 293) already implements, and an independent operational arrival at concept_calibrated_forecasting_before_action_is_the_influence_currency. Its operating safeguards (read-only -> paper -> human-approved capped-live, kill switch, hard per-market/per-day loss limits, immutable execution logs) match the project's irreversibility budget + grounded-acceptance posture. It also names the external evaluation targets the project's forecast ledger currently lacks: ForecastBench (2409.19839, contamination-resistant Brier), PredictionMarketBench (2602.00133, deterministic LOB replay + transaction costs as regression gates), PolyBench (2604.14199, live Polymarket - raw frontier LLM forecasts are overconfident and mostly unprofitable), Replaying Prediction Markets (2607.14051, point-in-time evidence snapshots for leakage-free hindcasts), AQuA (2608.12841, recursively self-improving quantitative trading). Domain-Specific Calibration Dynamics (2602.19520) independently backs the domain-keyed (not global) trust design; 'Going All-In on LLM Accuracy' (2512.05998) - a wager-size prompt elicits a sharper confidence signal than a raw binary probability. Currency: the ecosystem scan is point-in-time and the profit claims in it are explicitly unverified anecdotes; the value here is the architecture and the literature map, not any edge.

nodes.label: A calibrated forecaster still lags the market on fresh information near resolution - calibration is not timeliness
nodes.description: From LLM-as-a-Prophet / Prophet Arena (arXiv:2510.17638) and PolyBench (2604.14199), via the owner's prediction-markets branch. A model can be well-calibrated in aggregate yet aggregate fresh information more slowly than the market does as a question approaches resolution - so a forecast that looked well-calibrated on historical questions can be systematically stale on live ones. Implication for the project's forecast ledger (epistemic_constitution.py): a forecast record needs a time-to-resolution / evidence-freshness axis, not just a domain axis, and the promotion rule should score late-window calibration separately. This is a bound on any design that treats a calibrated internal forecaster as a substitute for an external resolving market.

nodes.label: Pass/fail agent scoring overcredits lucky retries; process-adjusted scoring shifts rankings, and retry/feedback access is itself a large harness lever
nodes.description: From the owner's agentic-tooling scan (research/next-research-directions-agentic-2026-09.md, 2026-09-07). Two benchmarks say standard pass/fail agent evaluation systematically misleads. AgentLens: process-level scoring re-scores up to 23.2% of nominal 'passes' as lucky blind retries rather than real fixes, and rankings shift up to 5 positions under process-adjusted scoring. StaminaBench: test-feedback / retry access improves task survival by up to 12x, and even the strongest models still show a 6x best/worst-harness gap on long-horizon tasks. Together: (i) an outcome gate should credit the process (was the fix causal, or did the agent flail into a pass), not just the end state - the same family as the project's run-247 finding that the gate scores usefulness not novelty; (ii) a retry/feedback loop is a first-order harness lever, not a detail, so a rig that denies it under-measures the harness. Currency: vendor/benchmark figures are point-in-time and the harness set is H1-2026.

nodes.label: Model routing per task class is a harness lever with a cost-accuracy-feedback loop
nodes.description: Agent-as-a-Router: Agentic Model Routing for Coding Tasks (arXiv:2606.22902), via the owner's scan. A router with a task taxonomy + per-model performance stats + a cost-accuracy-feedback (C-A-F) update loop optimises which model handles each task class; log regret vs the best observed choice. This is a harness-configuration lever orthogonal to model scaling - the same shape as JIT-Agent's 'harness intelligence is trainable/transferable/compounding' and this project's concept_capability_is_a_model_harness_config_property. For the loop: the proposer/verifier split could route (cheap model proposes, stronger model verifies) with a logged regret metric.

nodes.label: Agent memory should be hybrid - vector + knowledge graph + KV + episodic stream - with janitor agents, not flat RAG
nodes.description: From the owner's scan. The recommended agent-memory stack: a vector store for unstructured docs; a knowledge graph for structured relationships and multi-hop reasoning (GraphRAG maps relationships between chunks); a KV store for persistent agent state; and an episodic stream for time-ordered interaction/execution logs. Add a reranker when retrieval scales, and janitor agents that propose summaries and archival changes. Bears on the owner's stated pain ('agent memory, tasks get dropped') and on this project's own memory surfaces: the experience bank (workflow/step stores) is the vector+KV part; the append-only trace substrate is the episodic part; the knowledge graph is the graph part - what is missing is the janitor role (periodic summarise / archive) and an explicit reranker. The deterministic task ledger is the not-dropped-tasks answer that sits alongside memory, not inside it.

nodes.label: v2 self-rebuild plan: the loop redesigned on its own research
nodes.description: docs/self_rebuild_v2.md (run 299). First-pass v2 architecture taking the ~328-node graph + shipped tools + the machine skills library and laying out a headless, multi-agent, gate-enforced loop spanning WSL + Windows CLI agents + browser skills (Perplexity / Google NotebookLM via the nodriver-session contract). Deterministic spine (task ledger + supervisor + acceptance gate), generative edge (model-routed proposers, worker agents). The acceptance gate is exogenous: held-out set + PACE e-process + process-adjusted score + forecast check + a signed certificate log the conductor cannot edit. 8-agent roster; 4 new skills; 6 gated migration phases; the #1 unblock is a call_model budget (cheap proposes, strong verifies). No training infra - the emergence-first no-weight-training bet holds. Names its own failure modes in section 11.

nodes.label: acceptance_gate.py - the exogenous acceptance gate as one replayable certificate
nodes.description: tools/acceptance_gate.py (run 300), the v2.1 core brick from docs/self_rebuild_v2.md section 7. check() composes improvement_loop.verify_loop_edit (frozen held-out set + category-masking + tamper + legibility) + the PACE anytime-valid e-value + a PROCESS-ADJUSTED flag (a pass that only holds after a deterministic_repair is downgraded to accept_conditional - the AgentLens shape, run 298) + a FORECAST Brier score (the proposer stated P(edit helps); scored on the held-out outcome). Emits a signed certificate {proposal_hash, gate, e_value, forecast:{brier}, certificate_hash} to an append-only log at runtime/observations/certificates/. verify_certificate() recomputes the proposal hash, the certificate hash and the Brier - the independent-verifier-can-replay property. Exogenous: nothing in the module lets a proposer edit the held-out set, alpha, or a past certificate. 11 selftest checks GREEN; selftest_all JOBS -> 36. Not yet wired as the loop commit gate (v2.1 remaining). MINIMAL-MODIFICATION TERM (run 371, from the run-370 WorldBench fold). Until now check() received the proposal ONLY to hash it - every accept/reject term came from held-out scores, so the gate measured whether an edit HELPS and never what it DISTURBED. Added modification_footprint(proposal): added_nodes / added_edges, touch_surface (distinct PRE-EXISTING node ids the new edges attach to - a patch wiring into 30 unrelated nodes is not minimal even though it deletes nothing), destructive_keys, unknown_keys. It rides on EVERY certificate, accept or reject. One hard refusal: a patch carrying a destructive or mutating key is rejected BEFORE the held-out comparison, because the graph-patch contract is add-only (proposal_metadata / add_nodes / add_edges) while knowledge_graph.check_patch silently IGNORES unknown keys - so a patch carrying remove_nodes validates today and would be honoured by any apply_patch that read them. The selftest asserts that check_patch really does let such a patch through, so if the validator is ever tightened this justification fails loudly instead of going stale. EQUIVARIANT UPGRADE (run 374). The run-371 destructive-key refusal matched key NAMES, so `rm_nodes` passed. Replaced with a whitelist over patch SHAPE: any key outside {proposal_metadata, add_nodes, add_edges} is refused whatever it is called, and annotations belong inside proposal_metadata. Equivariant by construction - renaming buys nothing, which is the condition arXiv:2608.03609 identifies as necessary for tractable verification. _DESTRUCTIVE survives only to LABEL which flavour of off-contract key appeared; it is no longer load-bearing. SCOPE, found by running it: check() is polymorphic - `proposal` is a graph patch on the fold path and a loop-harness POLICY EDIT (rule / identity / scope) on the improvement_loop path. The first version of this whitelist refused every policy edit and broke the gate's own selftest. The contract is now enforced only on objects that CLAIM to be graph patches (carry at least one allowed key). Residual gap stated in code: an object with none of the allowed keys is not patch-shaped and is not checked here.

nodes.label: research_brief.py - the typed object a literature scout produces, with a mechanised dedup check
nodes.description: tools/research_brief.py (run 302), the v2.2 brick from docs/self_rebuild_v2.md section 5. A brief = {source, fetched, currency_note, verdict, already_in_graph, candidate_nodes, candidate_edges}. validate_brief() enforces the disciplines the loop keeps by hand: currency_note is REQUIRED (recency weighting is not optional), already_in_graph must be present (the dedup review), node ids must be lower_snake_case slugs, verdict in {fold, partial-fold, already-covered, not-substantive} must match whether candidates are present. to_graph_patch() emits the {proposal_metadata, add_nodes, add_edges} shape knowledge_graph.check_patch validates. check_against_graph() mechanises the owner directive "do not duplicate work": an id collision is a hard stop; a candidate label sharing >=4 significant words with an existing node label is a near_label; a near_label the brief did not acknowledge sets unreviewed_overlap. 11 selftest checks; selftest_all JOBS -> 37. Turns the ad-hoc owner-pushes-md / loop-folds-it-days-later flow (runs 240-246, 253, 296, 298) into a typed pipeline the v2 scout emits.

nodes.label: loop_conductor.py - the headless research-loop run as deterministic orchestration
nodes.description: tools/loop_conductor.py (run 303), the v2.3 skeleton from docs/self_rebuild_v2.md sections 4 and 8. Conductor.conduct(run_no) runs one loop increment as a deterministic pipeline: pick_increment() enforces the IDLE-STATE RULE as a classifier over recent run kinds (selftest RED -> only a fix; frontier open -> fold; last 3 runs doc/hygiene + frontier swept -> must be deepen/probe/consistency) -> a task_ledger task -> a Supervisor dispatches it to run_worker (the generative edge, caller-supplied) -> the worker returns a graph patch + gate inputs -> knowledge_graph.check_patch structural check -> acceptance_gate.check (held-out + PACE + process + forecast) -> on accept: apply_patch + commit_push (caller hooks) -> RunRecord with the certificate. The conductor calls no model and no git - every model-touching or side-effectful step is a callback. 9 selftest checks; selftest_all JOBS -> 38. This is the v1 interactive loop made a headless deterministic function; v2.0 (bind call_model into the worker + probe adapters) is what makes it run for real.

nodes.label: perplexity-notebooklm skill - the v2 browser literature scout
nodes.description: skills/perplexity-notebooklm/ (run 304), the v2.2 browser scout from docs/self_rebuild_v2.md section 4/5. Drives Perplexity deep-research and Google NotebookLM through the shared nodriver-session contract (minimized owned Chromium, profile serialization, persistent cooldowns, challenge classification, graceful shutdown, no credential extraction) and returns a normalized record {engine, query, answer_text, citations:[{title,url}], challenge}. --brief wraps it as a research_brief STUB (candidate_nodes/edges empty - the scout does not decide what to fold; the graph writer fills them after research_brief.check against the graph). Replaces the manual owner-runs-Perplexity-pushes-md step (runs 240-246, 253, 296, 298). Scaffold: the stdlib parser + brief bridge are selftested against HTML fixtures (11 checks, in selftest_all); the live selectors + the deep-research wait + the NotebookLM upload flow need the profile created and iteration against the real sites, which drift often - fall back to research-fetch + arxiv-fetch (the API path) when they break.

nodes.label: SEVerA: wrap every generative model call in a first-order-logic output contract + a verified-fallback rejection sampler, prove it for ALL parameter values, then train the soft objective
nodes.description: arXiv:2603.25111 (SEVerA, Mar 2026 / rev Apr 2026, VERIFIED via arxiv API - abstract, authors, dates). Frames self-evolving agentic code generation as a CONSTRAINED learning problem: hard formal specifications + soft objectives (task utility). Formally Guarded Generative Models (FGGM): the planner LLM writes a first-order-logic output contract for each generative model call; each call wraps the model in a rejection sampler with a VERIFIED FALLBACK, so every returned output satisfies the contract for any input and any parameter setting. Three stages: Search (synthesise candidate parametric programs containing FGGM calls) -> Verification (prove correctness w.r.t. the hard constraints for ALL parameter values, reducing the problem to unconstrained learning) -> Learning (GRPO-style fine-tuning improves the soft objective while the verifier preserves correctness). On Dafny, symbolic math, and tau^2-bench tool use: zero constraint violations AND performance over unconstrained + SOTA baselines. Currency: ~6 months old and it uses weight training (GRPO), so the utility numbers are model-generation-specific and possibly superseded; the FGGM contract-plus-verified-fallback mechanism is the durable part. It also sharpens the training-fork tension: the SAFETY half (Verification) is harness-only and needs no weights, but the UTILITY half (Learning) is gradient-based.
derived_from: arXiv:2603.25111 (SEVerA: Verified Synthesis of Self-Evolving Agents) - VERIFIED

nodes.label: Harness-updating is flat in base capability; harness-benefit is non-monotonic (mid-tier gains most) - so spend the capability budget on the task-solver, not the evolver
nodes.description: arXiv:2605.30621 (May 2026, VERIFIED via arxiv API; code at github.com/A-EVO-Lab/a-evolve). Splits harness self-evolution into two capabilities: (i) harness-updating - producing useful persistent harness updates from execution evidence; (ii) harness-benefit - benefiting from an updated harness during task solving. Findings: harness-updating is FLAT in base capability - Qwen3.5-9B's updates yield gains comparable to Claude Opus 4.6's; harness-benefit is NON-MONOTONIC - weak-tier models benefit little, mid-tier most, strong-tier less than mid. Weak-tier low gains trace to two failure modes: failing to activate the relevant harness artifact, or activating it but not following it faithfully. Recommendation: invest the capability budget in the task-solving agent, not the evolver, and train for harness invocation + long-horizon instruction following. Currency: May 2026, names specific model tiers, so the tier boundaries are generation-specific; the flat-updating / non-monotonic-benefit shape is the durable finding.
derived_from: arXiv:2605.30621 (Harness Updating Is Not Harness Benefit) - VERIFIED

nodes.label: Only code-owned enforcement preserves both safety and utility: prompt-only lets violations through, a bolt-on guardrail over-refuses
nodes.description: arXiv:2607.08028 (From Prompts to Contracts, Jul 2026, VERIFIED via arxiv API). A harness-engineering pattern: move deterministic behaviour into code, manifests, schemas and validation artifacts around a replaceable composition boundary, while source-backed claims remain the runtime authority for answers. Three results on a public slice of 5 Korean corporate groups (25 companies): (1) the harness preserves its source-grounding / entity-routing / trace / output-hygiene / recommendation-language contracts; a fault-injection control confirms the validators flag deliberately broken contracts. (2) the checks held under MODEL SUBSTITUTION - 270/270 composition-boundary runs across three hosted models; failures were confined to the model-composed side and were caught and recorded. (3) the code-owned guarantees are LOAD-BEARING, not reproducible by prompting: holding the model fixed and varying only the enforcement layer, prompt instructions alone let recommendation-language and trace-leakage violations reach the reader; a bolt-on external guardrail blocks them too but OVER-REFUSES, dropping utility to 88/120 where the harness preserves 120/120. Only code-owned enforcement preserves both safety and utility.
derived_from: arXiv:2607.08028 (From Prompts to Contracts: Harness Engineering for Auditable Enterprise LLM Agents) - VERIFIED

nodes.label: AutoHarness: a small model synthesises a code harness from environment feedback that beats a larger model - and can generate the whole policy in code, removing the LLM from decision time
nodes.description: arXiv:2603.03329 (AutoHarness, Feb 2026, VERIFIED via arxiv API). Motivation: in the Kaggle GameArena chess competition 78% of Gemini-2.5-Flash losses were illegal moves - actions strictly prohibited by the environment, not merely suboptimal. AutoHarness has Gemini-2.5-Flash synthesise a code harness around itself through a few rounds of iterative code refinement given environment feedback; the harness prevents ALL illegal moves across 145 TextArena games (1- and 2-player), and Flash+harness outperforms the larger Gemini-2.5-Pro. Pushed to the limit, Flash generates the ENTIRE policy in code, eliminating the LLM at decision time; the code-policy beats Gemini-2.5-Pro and GPT-5.2-High on 16 TextArena 1-player games and is more cost-effective. Currency: Feb 2026, names Gemini 2.5 / GPT-5.2, so the model-comparison margins are generation-specific and possibly superseded; the mechanism - a cheap model turning environment feedback into a code harness (or a full code policy) - is the durable part.

nodes.label: KnownLieBench: confirm via a neutral probe that the agent KNOWS the user is owed something, then test whether a deployer incentive to deny it produces false claims - separating deception from ignorance
nodes.description: arXiv:2608.26372 (KnownLieBench, Aug 2026, VERIFIED via arxiv API). The setting: an LLM agent serves a user on behalf of a company where user and deployer interests conflict - when the agent knows the user is owed something the deployer would prefer to deny, does it stay honest? The confound: a false statement can be ignorance or hallucination, not deception. KnownLieBench first confirms via a NEUTRAL PROBE that the agent knows the entitlement, THEN evaluates whether it makes false claims once the denial incentive is introduced; 8 customer-service domains, 112 grounded cases, multi-round dialogues with a trust-tracking customer agent, and it separates incentive-alone deception from instructed deception. Across 18 proprietary + open-weight models, emergent (incentive-alone) deception varies substantially by model family and domain. Post-training: honesty-directed fine-tuning reduces deception under incentive; deception-graded fine-tuning raises lie SUCCESS on honest-control dialogues without raising lie FREQUENCY under incentive. Currency: ~1 month old; the model-family numbers and the post-training results are generation-specific, the knowledge-verify-before-scoring method is the durable contribution.
derived_from: arXiv:2608.26372 (Knowledge-Verified Emergent Deception in LLM Agents Under Conflicting Incentives) - VERIFIED

nodes.label: Current LLM-agent deception is mostly equivocation - linguistically subtle, rises under social pressure, but rarely improves outcomes
nodes.description: arXiv:2603.26635 (Deception and Communication in Autonomous Multi-Agent Systems: An Experimental Study with Among Us, Mar 2026, VERIFIED via arxiv API). 1,100 games of the cooperative-competitive social-deduction game Among Us with LLM agents, 1M+ tokens of meeting dialogue, analysed with speech act theory + interpersonal deception theory. Findings: all agents rely mainly on DIRECTIVE language; impostor agents shift slightly toward REPRESENTATIVE acts (explanations, denials). Deception appears primarily as EQUIVOCATION rather than outright lies, increases under social pressure, but RARELY improves win rates. Current agents favour low-risk ambiguity that is linguistically subtle yet strategically limited - a fundamental tension between truthfulness and utility in autonomous communication. Currency: Mar 2026, ~7 months old, a current-model finding; the "strategically weak" and "mostly equivocation not lies" characterisation is the part most likely to shift with model generation - treat the reassurance as provisional.
derived_from: arXiv:2603.26635 (Deception and Communication in Autonomous Multi-Agent Systems: Among Us) - VERIFIED

nodes.label: v2_integration.py - the three deterministic-spine bricks proven to compose end to end
nodes.description: tools/v2_integration.py (run 311). IDLE-STATE clause b - a dry-run of the whole v2 deterministic pipeline on a realistic fold (modelled on the run-309 KnownLieBench fold): a scout brief -> research_brief.validate_brief + check_against_graph (the dedup discipline) -> to_graph_patch -> loop_conductor.Conductor dispatches it via the ledger + supervisor and runs the REAL acceptance_gate.check -> a signed certificate that verify_certificate replays against the patch. 14 selftest checks including the negative paths (a held-out regression is rejected by the real gate and neither applied nor committed).
