MaMa designs the system against a worst-case adversary at design time rather than giving agents room and observing. A mild pull toward control-first - though the design SEARCH is open-ended, and the result generalises beyond the training adversary, which is the emergence-first hope.

Run 283 dry-run (sweep): composed design extends the usable horizon 12 -> 24 steps vs prose handoffs, but the base per-step failure rate still sets a ceiling - "you need short TASKS, not just short agents". Fractal decomposition is the mechanism that makes tasks short: spawn a child only for an unresolved boundary and keep each context narrow, so the per-step rate applies over fewer steps per agent.

Geometric decay caps any long trajectory (~16 steps to collapse). Fractal decomposition responds by keeping every agent trajectory short and problem-shaped - deep only where the task is genuinely unresolved - so no single agent runs long enough to hit the decay wall.

Run 284 dry-run: AUC 1.0 in-distribution vs 0.716 on emergent-untrained collusion (gap 0.284) - "a detector for the assigned scenario, not an observation channel". Extends the run-278 finding beyond LLM-as-judge: even the activation-probe channel does not generalise from assigned to emergent collusion, so behavioural-regret metrics are more necessary, not less.

Run 284 dry-run: a self-preferring evaluator reports a 0.218 gain; only 0.073 (33.5%) survives on held-out. That 3x inflation is exactly why influence must be earned by CALIBRATED prediction scored against later ground truth, not by an agent reporting its own gain.

The runnable numbers for the claim: honest selection would have captured 0.095 held-out gain; the self-preference winner captures 0.073 - the evaluator that scores itself picks a worse edit AND reports a better number.
The runnable test of the claim: calibration-record selection beats manager-pick and debate at every persuasion level and does not degrade as persuasion rises, where the confidence-reading rules do.
First runnable evidence for the parent: pricing by track record rather than by current agreement is what keeps the group accurate when agreement collapses into a cascade.

Quantifies the trade: majority vote is the BEST rule (Condorcet) as long as errors stay independent - it is only worth replacing when votes become visible and cascade (-0.15 here). The herding node is the necessity condition for the epistemic market.

FORECAST wins under herding only because it elicits INDEPENDENTLY (reads each agents own answer, not the cascaded pool) - which is exactly the evidence-cell protocol. Without independent elicitation, calibration selection also gets the herded answer.
A concrete SELECTION-side instance of the run-218 criterion: the aggregation rule (not a vote) is what determines whether a multi-agent pool beats a single strong agent.

The runnable sweep of the protocol step: identity-masked synthesis. Quantifies which cues matter - the reasoning chain leaks more status than the name - and shows the protocol needs INDEPENDENT elicitation on top of masking to close the last 0.03 accuracy gap.

Operationalises the finding: a PEER_RECOGNITION_FLOOR that no masking level removes leaves 0.16 residual deference at L3. Full masking is necessary but not sufficient - matches the anonymization node.
Adds a lever to the herding node: what is shown alongside a vote (name / style / reasoning) determines how much it herds. Stripping the reasoning chain matters more than stripping the name.

The two epistemic-market rigs compose: probe_epistemic_market shows forecast-selection needs independent elicitation to beat herding; probe_identity_masking shows masking alone (even full) does not achieve independence - you need both.

The runnable test: pre-registration lifts factual accuracy +0.16 over reflection and +0.15 over open debate, while its creativity cost (-0.12 vs reflection) is smaller than the gain. Open debate is floor-raising only (no net reliability gain, large creativity cost).

Quantifies the within-run exploration-to-exploitation cost per protocol: open debate (fast convergence) explores 0.38 of the idea space, pre-registration (adversarial framing delays convergence) explores 0.58, reflection 0.70. The decline is protocol-dependent, and pre-registration slows it.
Evidence for the parent claim that debate is the wrong default: open debate here neither raises reliability nor preserves creativity; a pre-registered, evidence-led protocol does both.

Third epistemic-market rig: probe_epistemic_market (selection), probe_identity_masking (elicitation independence), probe_adversarial_collaboration (dispute resolution) cover the three moments the cluster touches.
A concrete instance: cooperation/emergence peak at medium environmental pressure - here net system value peaks at a medium red-team challenge rate (r~0.5), collapsing at both ends.

Supports risk-proportionate friction: challenge is worth applying, but only up to the paralysis knee - the same logic the irreversibility budget applies to irreversible actions, applied to review load.
A permanent red-team institution (part5 #48) needs a rate cap: unbounded challenge authority freezes the system it governs. The rig gives the cap a shape (interior optimum, sharp fall past the knee).

The runnable test of the domain-keyed claim, sharpened: strict per-family trust (no transfer) predicts held-out families at chance, and universal trust overclaims + concentrates authority. The working middle is similarity-weighted transfer - trust IS domain-keyed, but the keys have a similarity metric.

Emergent reputation tends to a single social-status scalar (authority concentration 1.00 here). The rig shows that scalar predicts a NEW task family only at +0.49 - well below what its universal claim implies - so a scalar reputation systematically over-grants authority.

The epistemic market routes by trust (probe_epistemic_market); this rig says the trust graph it routes on must be similarity-keyed, not a scalar - otherwise routing concentrates on one agent regardless of the task family.

probe_adversarial_collaboration compares dissent vs reflection on a SINGLE task; this rig compounds the comparison over a HORIZON-round evolution and shows the advantage widens - a single-round net of +0.03 becomes +0.20 at h=40.

Operationalises the format-repair finding as a compounding drift: a self-score with an optimism bias accepts negative edits, and over a long horizon reflection reaches q 0.72 where an unbiased head-to-head reaches 0.98.

The rig is an acceptor comparison: a biased acceptor (reflection self-score) vs an unbiased one (dissent head-to-head). Confirms the acceptor is the weak point - same proposer, different acceptor, 0.26 quality gap at h=40.
Recursive meta-improvement needs an unbiased acceptor at each level or the drift compounds through the recursion; structured dissent is a concrete unbiased acceptor.
The runnable test of whether a domain-keyed trust graph counters herding: it recovers ~31% of the cascade loss, and a wrong-family (stale) trust graph recovers ~3% - the domain key is load-bearing.

Bounds the mitigation: trust-weighting the vote helps (kill condition does not hold) but the majority-following is not prevented - the herded answers are still wrong, trust only down-weights the herders. Removing the vote entirely (probe_epistemic_market forecast-selection) does better.

Completes the epistemic-market rig set: probe_epistemic_market (forecast-selection removes the vote), probe_identity_masking (elicitation independence), probe_adversarial_collaboration (dispute resolution), probe_trust_transfer (the trust graph transfers), probe_trust_weighted_voting (trust-weighting a vote is a partial fix). All 5 point at the same conclusion - independent elicitation + calibration-weighting, not a raw vote.
The parent claim made runnable: agents interact through structured falsifiable claim objects priced by a calibration record, not by messages or votes. This is the deterministic core of that market.

The forecast ledger IS this concept: predict before acting, score Brier on resolve, derive influence from the record. probe_epistemic_market (286) validated that this beats manager-pick / debate / self-score.
trust(agent, domain) = 1 - mean Brier in that domain; no cross-domain leak, cold start = None. probe_trust_transfer (290) showed a global scalar over-grants authority; this refuses to compute one.
Same discipline as the task ledger (deterministic, atomic write, audit log) applied to CLAIMS and FORECASTS rather than tasks - the epistemic source of truth alongside the orchestration one.
The promotion rule is a grounded acceptance gate for claims: a Brier threshold + independent replication + counterexample survival, none of which an agent can self-report past.
Puts the rigor on the acceptor: a claim is promoted by its calibration record and replication, not by who proposed it or how well they argued.

The prototype the 7 rigs point at: probe_epistemic_market / _identity_masking / _adversarial_collaboration / _trust_transfer / _dissent_vs_reflection / _trust_weighted_voting each validated one mechanism this module composes.
The concept made runnable: no orchestrator, coordination is a shared append-only artifact store read through a bounded peer neighbourhood.
The spawn rule is exactly this concept: a node expands ONLY on returned unresolved_boundaries, depth- and count-bounded, and the completed subtree is compressed to a summary.
The prototype the run-273 flock arm points at: stigmergic accretion with bounded neighbourhoods is a viable integration mode; this is a deterministic substrate for running it.
Same discipline (deterministic, atomic write, audit log) applied to a TREE of contributions with adaptive depth rather than a flat task list.
The compress step is per-consumer trace compilation at each recursion boundary: the parent consumes a one-line summary of the child subtree, not its full contribution history.
probe_composed_design (283): you need short TASKS not just short agents. The fractal spawn keeps every node bounded and problem-shaped, and compresses on return - short tasks by construction.
The module is the deterministic spine (store, spawn rule, compression, audit); contribute() is the generative edge. Agents create freely inside a node; the coordination is not theirs to change.

One of the branch's own headline literature findings (Prophet Arena, PolyBench) - included here as the sharpest design constraint it carries.

Both: a standard agent benchmark number is not what it looks like - contamination inflates it from one side, uncredited lucky retries from another.

JIT-Agent argues harness intelligence is trainable and compounding. 2605.30621 finds the harness-updating capability is already flat across capability tiers, so training a stronger EVOLVER has low marginal return - the compounding, if any, is on the task-solver side.

A large measured delta of the favourable kind: the same small model gains enough from a synthesised harness to overtake a larger bare model.
